title.zh: 卷一百八十七 列傳第一百十二 二王諸葛李孟
title.en: Volume 187 Biographies 112: Two Wangs, Zhu, Ge, Li, Meng
title.raw: 卷一百八十七 列傳第一百十二 二王諸葛李孟 Volume 187 Biographies 112: Two Wangs, Zhu, Ge, Li, Meng

sentences.zh: 二王諸葛李孟

translations.literal: The Two Wangs, Zhu, Ge, Li, and Meng
translations.idiomatic: The Two Wangs, Zhu, Ge, Li, and Meng

sentences.zh: 王重榮，太原祁人。

translations.literal: Wang Chongrong was a man of Qi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父縱，太和末為河中騎將，從石雄破回鶻，終鹽州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Zong, at the end of the Taihe era served as a cavalry officer in Hezhong, followed Shi Xiong in defeating the Uyghurs, and ended as governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zong, in the closing years of the Taihe reign, served as a cavalry officer in Hezhong; he followed Shi Xiong against the Uyghurs and eventually became governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 重榮以父任為列校，與兄重盈皆以毅武冠軍，擢河中牙將，主伺察。

translations.literal: Chongrong, through his father's position, became a company commander; he and his elder brother Chongying both were foremost in the army for resolute martial prowess, and were promoted to Hezhong garrison officers in charge of surveillance.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's influence Chongrong entered service as a company commander. He and his elder brother Chongying were famed for their martial resolve and were promoted to Hezhong garrison officers charged with surveillance.

sentences.zh: 時兩軍士幹夜禁，捕而鞭之。

translations.literal: At the time soldiers of the two armies violated the night curfew; he seized and flogged them.
translations.idiomatic: When soldiers from the two armies broke the night curfew, he seized them and had them flogged.

sentences.zh: 士還，訴於中尉楊玄實，玄實怒，執重榮讓曰：「天子爪士，而藩校辱之！」

translations.literal: The soldiers returned and complained to the superintendent Yang Xuanshi. Xuanshi was angry, seized Chongrong and rebuked him, saying, "The Son of Heaven's claw troops, and a frontier commander insults them!
translations.idiomatic: The men went back and complained to the superintendent Yang Xuanshi. Enraged, Xuanshi seized Chongrong and rebuked him: "These are the Son of Heaven's own troops—how dare a frontier officer humiliate them!

sentences.zh: 答曰：「夜半執者奸盜，孰知天子爪士？」

translations.literal: He replied, "Those seized at midnight were thieves and bandits—who knew they were the Son of Heaven's claw troops?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Those I seized in the middle of the night were thieves and bandits—how was anyone to know they were the Son of Heaven's own troops?"

sentences.zh: 具言其狀。

translations.literal: He set forth the circumstances in full.
translations.idiomatic: He then explained the whole affair in detail.

sentences.zh: 玄實嘆曰：「非爾明辨，孰由知之？」

translations.literal: Xuanshi sighed and said, "Had you not been so discerning, who would have known?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuanshi sighed and said, "If you had not seen so clearly, who would ever have known?

sentences.zh: 更諉於府，擢右署。

translations.literal: He shifted the blame to the commandery and promoted Chongrong to the right office.
translations.idiomatic: He redirected the complaint to the commandery headquarters and promoted Chongrong to a post in the right office.

sentences.zh: 重榮多權詭，眾所嚴憚，雖主帥莫不下之。

translations.literal: Chongrong was full of schemes and stratagems; all held him in awe, and even the commander did not look down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong was cunning and resourceful, and everyone feared him—even the commander treated him with deference.

sentences.zh: 稍遷行軍司馬。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to campaigning marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to campaigning marshal.

sentences.zh: 黃巢陷長安，分兵略蒲，節度使李都不能支，乃臣賊，然內憚重榮，表以自副。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao took Chang'an, he sent troops to overrun Pu. The military governor Li Du could not hold out, so he submitted to the rebels, yet inwardly he feared Chongrong and memorialized to make him his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: After Huang Chao seized Chang'an, he sent forces to overrun Pu. Military Governor Li Du could not resist and submitted to the rebels, but he feared Chongrong inwardly and memorialized to appoint him his deputy.

sentences.zh: 地邇京師，賊調取橫數，使者至百輩，坐傳舍，益發兵，吏不堪命。

translations.literal: The territory lay near the capital; the rebels levied exactions at will. Envoys came by the hundreds, lodged at relay stations, and demanded ever more troops—the clerks could not bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: Because the region lay close to the capital, the rebels extorted supplies at will. Envoys arrived in hundreds, lodged at relay stations, and kept demanding more troops until the officials were overwhelmed.

sentences.zh: 重榮脅說都曰：「我所詭謀紓難，以外援未至。

translations.literal: Chongrong coerced and persuaded Du, saying, "My stratagems have eased our difficulties only because outside aid has not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong pressed Du, saying, "My schemes have bought us time only because outside help has not yet come.

sentences.zh: 今賊裒責日急，又收吾兵以困我，則亡無日矣。

translations.literal: Now the rebels' exactions grow daily more urgent, and they are also taking our troops to hem us in—then destruction will come any day.
translations.idiomatic: Now their demands grow harsher by the day, and they are also stripping away our troops to strangle us—we will not last another day.

sentences.zh: 請絕橋，嬰城自守，不然，變生何以制之？」

translations.literal: I beg that we cut the bridges and hold the city behind closed gates; otherwise, when trouble arises, how will we control it?
translations.idiomatic: Cut the bridges and hold the city behind closed gates. Otherwise, once trouble breaks out, how will we control it?

sentences.zh: 都曰：「吾兵寡，謀不足，絕之，禍且至，願以節假公。」

translations.literal: Du said, "My troops are few and my plans insufficient; if we cut them off, disaster will soon come. I wish to lend you my commissioner's seal."
translations.idiomatic: Du said, "My forces are few and my counsel weak. If we cut them off, disaster will follow at once. I will lend you my authority as military commissioner."

sentences.zh: 遂奔行在。

translations.literal: He then fled to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: With that he fled to join the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 重榮乃悉驅出賊使斬之，因大掠居人以悅其下。

translations.literal: Chongrong then drove out all the rebel envoys and beheaded them, and on that pretext plundered the inhabitants greatly to please his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong then expelled every rebel envoy and had them beheaded, then plundered the townspeople on a large scale to win over his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 天子使前京兆尹竇潏間道慰其軍，因詔代都。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent the former metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, Dou Fu, by a secret route to comfort his army, and issued an edict to replace Du.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the former Jingzhao metropolitan magistrate Dou Fu by a hidden route to reassure the army and issued an edict replacing Du.

sentences.zh: 重榮率官屬奉迎。

translations.literal: Chongrong led the officials in welcoming him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong led the officials out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 潏至，大饗士，倡言曰：「天子以大臣守土，誰得逐之？

translations.literal: When Fu arrived, he held a great feast for the troops and proclaimed, "The Son of Heaven appoints great ministers to guard the land—who may drive them out?
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Fu arrived, he feasted the troops and declared, "The Son of Heaven appoints great ministers to guard the realm—who dares drive one out?

sentences.zh: 為我疏首惡者。」

translations.literal: Name for me the chief culprit."
translations.idiomatic: Point out the ringleader for me.

sentences.zh: 眾無敢對。

translations.literal: No one dared answer.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared speak.

sentences.zh: 重榮佩刀歷階曰：「首謀者，我也，尚誰索？」

translations.literal: Chongrong, sword at his belt, mounted the steps and said, "The chief plotter is I—whom else do you seek?"
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong, sword at his belt, strode up the steps and said, "I am the ringleader—whom else are you looking for?

sentences.zh: 目潏，吏趣具騎，潏即奔還。

translations.literal: He fixed his gaze on Fu; the clerks hurried to ready horses, and Fu at once fled back.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed his eyes on Dou Fu. Clerks rushed to saddle horses, and Fu fled at once.

sentences.zh: 重榮遂主留後。

translations.literal: Chongrong then took charge as acting military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong thereupon assumed control as acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 賊使健將朱溫以舟師下馮翊，黃鄴率眾自華陰合攻重榮。

translations.literal: The rebels sent their stalwart general Zhu Wen with a fleet down to Tong Prefecture; Huang Ye led his forces from Huayin to join in attacking Chongrong.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent their able general Zhu Wen with a naval force down the Tong route, while Huang Ye led troops from Huayin to join the assault on Chongrong.

sentences.zh: 重榮感勵士眾，大戰，敗之，賊棄糧仗四十餘艘。

translations.literal: Chongrong inspired and exhorted the troops, fought a great battle, and defeated them; the rebels abandoned grain and weapons on more than forty vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong roused his men and fought a major engagement, routing the enemy; the rebels abandoned grain and arms on more than forty boats.

sentences.zh: 即拜檢校工部尚書，為節度使。

translations.literal: He was at once appointed acting Minister of Works and made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately appointed acting Minister of Works and confirmed as military governor.

sentences.zh: 會忠武監軍楊復光率陳、蔡兵萬人屯武功，重榮與連和，擊賊將李詳於華州，執以徇。

translations.literal: It happened that the Zhongwu army supervisor Yang Fuguang led ten thousand Chen and Cai troops and encamped at Wugong; Chongrong joined forces with him, attacked the rebel general Li Xiang at Huazhou, seized him, and paraded him in punishment.
translations.idiomatic: About then the Zhongwu army supervisor Yang Fuguang brought ten thousand Chen and Cai troops to camp at Wugong. Chongrong allied with him, struck the rebel general Li Xiang at Huazhou, captured him, and had him displayed as a warning.

sentences.zh: 賊使尚讓來攻，而朱溫將勁兵居前，敗重榮兵於西關門，於是出兵夏陽，掠河中漕米數十艘。

translations.literal: The rebels sent Shang Rang to attack, while Zhu Wen led crack troops in the van and defeated Chongrong's army at the West Pass Gate; they then sent troops out from Xiayang and seized dozens of Hezhong grain-transport vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent Shang Rang to attack, with Zhu Wen's elite troops in the van; they defeated Chongrong's force at the West Pass Gate, then marched from Xiayang and seized dozens of Hezhong grain convoys.

sentences.zh: 重榮選兵三萬攻溫，溫懼，悉鑿舟沈於河，遂舉同州降。

translations.literal: Chongrong selected thirty thousand troops to attack Wen. Wen was afraid, scuttled all his boats by sinking them in the river, and then surrendered Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong picked thirty thousand men to attack Zhu Wen. Terrified, Wen scuttled his entire fleet in the river and surrendered Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 復光欲斬之，重榮曰：「今招賊，一切釋罪。

translations.literal: Fuguang wished to execute him. Chongrong said, "Now we are recruiting rebels—all are pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang wanted to execute him, but Chongrong said, "We are now recruiting defectors from the rebels—everyone is to be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 且溫武銳可用，殺之不祥。」

translations.literal: Moreover Wen is martial and sharp and can be used; to kill him would be inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Wen is bold and capable—killing him would be an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 表為同華節度使。

translations.literal: He memorialized to make him military governor of Tong and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to appoint him military governor of Tong and Hua.

sentences.zh: 有詔即副河中行營招討，賜名全忠。

translations.literal: An edict at once made him deputy to the Hezhong campaigning army's pacification commissioner, and bestowed the name Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict immediately named him deputy to the Hezhong campaigning pacification commissioner and granted him the name Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 巢喪二州，怒甚，自將精兵數萬壁梁田。

translations.literal: Chao had lost two prefectures and was greatly enraged; he personally led tens of thousands of elite troops and fortified at Liangtian.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost two prefectures, Huang Chao was furious and personally led tens of thousands of elite troops to fortify at Liangtian.

sentences.zh: 重榮軍華陰，復光軍渭北，掎角攻之，賊大敗，執其將趙璋，巢中流矢走。

translations.literal: Chongrong encamped at Huayin, Fuguang at north of the Wei—they attacked in pincer fashion, the rebels were greatly defeated, their general Zhao Zhang was captured, and Chao was struck by an arrow and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong camped at Huayin while Fuguang held north of the Wei; attacking in concert they routed the rebels, captured the general Zhao Zhang, and Huang Chao was wounded by an arrow and fled.

sentences.zh: 重榮兵亦死耗相當。

translations.literal: Chongrong's troops also suffered deaths and losses in equal measure.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong's army likewise suffered casualties on a comparable scale.

sentences.zh: 懼巢復振，憂之，與復光計，復光曰：「我世與李克用共憂患，其人忠不顧難，死義如己。

translations.literal: Fearing that Chao would rise again, he was anxious and consulted with Fuguang. Fuguang said, "For generations my family and Li Keyong have shared hardships; the man is loyal and heedless of danger, and would die for righteousness as for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Huang Chao might rally again, he was deeply worried and consulted Fuguang, who said, "My family and Li Keyong have shared hardship for generations. He is loyal, fearless in danger, and would die for righteousness as readily as for himself.

sentences.zh: 若乞師焉，事蔑不濟。」

translations.literal: If we beg troops of him, the affair will surely succeed."
translations.idiomatic: If we ask him for troops, nothing will fail.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使者約連和。

translations.literal: They then sent envoys to arrange a joint alliance.
translations.idiomatic: They sent envoys to arrange a joint alliance.

sentences.zh: 克用使陳景斯總兵自嵐、石赴河中，親率師從之，遂平巢，復京師。

translations.literal: Keyong sent Chen Jingsi to command troops from Lan and Shi to hurry to Hezhong, and personally led his army after them; they then pacified Chao and recovered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent Chen Jingsi to lead forces from Lan and Shi to Hezhong and followed with his own army, defeating Huang Chao and recovering the capital.

sentences.zh: 以功檢校太尉、同中書門下平章事，封瑯邪郡王。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed acting Grand Preceptor, Grand Councilor with the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Prince of Langye Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was made acting Grand Preceptor and Grand Councilor, and enfeoffed as Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 累加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to acting Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to acting Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 中人田令孜怒重榮據鹽池之饒。

translations.literal: The eunuch Tian Lingzi was angry that Chongrong held the rich salt ponds.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Tian Lingzi was enraged that Chongrong controlled the lucrative salt ponds.

sentences.zh: 於時巨盜甫定，國用大覂，諸軍無所仰，而令孜為神策軍使，建請二池領屬鹽鐵，佐軍食。

translations.literal: At the time the great bandits had just been pacified, state revenue was greatly depleted, and the armies had nothing to rely on; Lingzi was director of the Shence Army and proposed that the two ponds be placed under the Salt and Iron Commission to supplement army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The great rebellion had only just been suppressed, state revenue was exhausted, and the armies had nowhere to turn. As director of the Shence Army, Lingzi proposed placing both salt ponds under the Salt and Iron Commission to help feed the troops.

sentences.zh: 重榮不許，奏言：「故事，歲輸鹽三千乘於有司，則斥所餘以贍軍。」

translations.literal: Chongrong would not agree and memorialized, "By precedent, three thousand cartloads of salt are delivered yearly to the authorities; what remains is then used to support the army."
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong refused and memorialized: "By established practice, three thousand cartloads of salt are delivered to the authorities each year, and the remainder is used to support the army.

sentences.zh: 天子遣使者諭旨，不聽。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent envoys to convey the imperial will, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to convey his will, but Chongrong would not comply.

sentences.zh: 令孜徙重榮兗海節度使，以王處存代之，詔克用將兵援河中。

translations.literal: Lingzi transferred Chongrong to be military governor of Yan and Hai, replaced him with Wang Chucun, and ordered Keyong to lead troops to reinforce Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi transferred Chongrong to Yan and Hai and replaced him with Wang Chucun, while ordering Li Keyong to march troops to reinforce Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 重榮上書劾令孜離間方鎮。

translations.literal: Chongrong submitted a memorial impeaching Lingzi for sowing discord among the frontier commands.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong memorialized the throne, accusing Lingzi of driving wedges between the frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 令孜遣邠寧朱玫進討，壁沙苑。

translations.literal: Lingzi sent the Binning commander Zhu Mei to advance in punitive attack, and he fortified at Shayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi sent the Binning commander Zhu Mei against him, and Mei fortified at Shayuan.

sentences.zh: 重榮詒克用書，且言：「奉密詔，須公到，使我圖公。

translations.literal: Chongrong sent a deceitful letter to Keyong, saying moreover, "I have received a secret edict: when you arrive, I am to plot against you.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong sent Li Keyong a forged letter claiming, "I have received a secret edict: once you arrive, I am to plot against you.

sentences.zh: 此令孜、朱全忠、朱玫之惑上也。」

translations.literal: This is Tian Lingzi, Zhu Quanzhong, and Zhu Mei misleading the court."
translations.idiomatic: This is Tian Lingzi, Zhu Quanzhong, and Zhu Mei misleading the throne.

sentences.zh: 因示偽詔。

translations.literal: He then displayed a forged edict.
translations.idiomatic: He then produced a forged edict as proof.

sentences.zh: 克用方與全忠有隙，信之，請討全忠及玫。

translations.literal: Keyong was then at odds with Quanzhong, believed it, and requested permission to attack Quanzhong and Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong was already at odds with Quanzhong, believed the letter, and asked permission to attack Quanzhong and Mei.

sentences.zh: 帝數詔和解。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly issued edicts urging reconciliation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly issued edicts calling for reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 克用合河中兵戰沙苑，玫大敗，奔邠州。

translations.literal: Keyong combined with Hezhong troops and fought at Shayuan; Mei was greatly defeated and fled to Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong joined Hezhong forces and fought at Shayuan; Mei was routed and fled to Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 神策軍潰還京師，遂大掠。

translations.literal: The Shence Army collapsed and returned to the capital, whereupon they plundered on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: The Shence Army broke and fell back on the capital, then looted the city on a vast scale.

sentences.zh: 克用乘勝西，天子走鳳翔。

translations.literal: Keyong pressed his victory westward; the Son of Heaven fled to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong pressed westward in victory, and the emperor fled to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 俄嗣襄王煴僭位，重榮不受命，與克用謀定王室。

translations.literal: Soon the heir Prince of Xiang, Yun, usurped the throne; Chongrong did not accept his orders and joined Keyong in plotting to settle the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the heir Prince of Xiang, Yun, seized the throne in pretense. Chongrong refused to obey him and joined Keyong in a plan to restore the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 楊復恭代令孜領神策，故與克用善，遣諫議大夫劉崇望賫詔諭天子意，兩人聽命，即獻縑十萬，願討玫自贖。

translations.literal: Yang Fugong replaced Lingzi in leading the Shence Army and was therefore on good terms with Keyong; he sent Remonstrance Grandee Liu Chongwang bearing an edict to convey the Son of Heaven's intent. The two obeyed, at once presented one hundred thousand bolts of silk, and wished to attack Mei to redeem themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fugong had replaced Lingzi as head of the Shence Army and was friendly with Keyong; he sent Remonstrance Grandee Liu Chongwang with an edict explaining the emperor's wishes. Both men submitted, immediately offered one hundred thousand bolts of silk, and volunteered to attack Zhu Mei to atone.

sentences.zh: 崇望還，群臣皆賀。

translations.literal: When Chongwang returned, all the ministers congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chongwang returned, the court officials all offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 重榮遂斬煴，長安復平。

translations.literal: Chongrong then beheaded Yun, and Chang'an was pacified again.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong then executed Yun, and Chang'an was restored to order.

sentences.zh: 然性悍酷，多殺戮，少縱舍。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was fierce and cruel, given to much killing and little mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by nature he was brutal and merciless, quick to kill and slow to forgive.

sentences.zh: 嘗植大木河上，內設機軸，有忤意者，輒置其上，機發皆溺。

translations.literal: He once planted a great timber in the river with a mechanism inside; whoever displeased him was placed upon it, the mechanism released, and all were drowned.
translations.idiomatic: He once set a great timber in the river fitted with a hidden mechanism; anyone who crossed him was placed on it, the trap released, and all were drowned.

sentences.zh: 嘗辱部將常行儒，行儒怨之。

translations.literal: He once humiliated his subordinate general Chang Xingru; Xingru bore a grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: He once humiliated his subordinate Chang Xingru, who came to hate him for it.

sentences.zh: 光啟三年，引兵夜攻府，重榮亡出外，詰旦殺之，推立重盈。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangqi, he led troops by night to attack the headquarters; Chongrong fled outside, and at dawn they killed him and installed Chongying.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangqi he led a night assault on headquarters. Chongrong fled the compound; at dawn they killed him and installed his brother Chongying.

sentences.zh: 重盈前此已歷汾州刺史。

translations.literal: Chongying had previously served as governor of Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chongying had earlier served as governor of Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 黃巢度淮，擢陜虢觀察使，重榮據河中，三遷檢校尚書右仆射，即拜節度使。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao crossed the Huai, he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Shan and Guo; while Chongrong held Hezhong, he was thrice promoted to acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, and then appointed military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao crossed the Huai, he was made surveillance commissioner of Shan and Guo. While his brother held Hezhong, he was promoted three times to acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and then confirmed as military governor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he became Grand Councilor with the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 及代重榮，留長子珙領節度事，入殺行儒，軍復安。

translations.literal: When he replaced Chongrong, he left his eldest son Gong to oversee military affairs, entered and killed Xingru, and the army was pacified again.
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded Chongrong, he left his eldest son Gong in charge of military affairs, entered headquarters and killed Xingru, and the army settled down again.

sentences.zh: 昭宗立，進太傅、兼中書令，封瑯邪郡王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong ascended, he was advanced to Grand Tutor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Prince of Langye Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong came to the throne, he was promoted to Grand Tutor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 父子兄弟相繼帥守，而從子蘊亦為忠武節度使。

translations.literal: Father, sons, and brothers succeeded one another as commanders and defenders, while his nephew Yun also became military governor of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Father, sons, and brothers held command in succession, and his nephew Yun also became military governor of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年，重盈死，軍中以其兄重簡子珂出繼重榮，故推為留後。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianning, Chongying died; the army, because his elder brother Chongjian's son Ke had been adopted to succeed Chongrong, therefore installed him as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianning Chongying died. Because his elder brother Chongjian's son Ke had been adopted to continue Chongrong's line, the army installed him as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 珙與弟絳州刺史瑤爭河中，上言：「珂本家蒼頭，請選大臣鎮河中。」

translations.literal: Gong and his younger brother Yao, governor of Jiang Prefecture, contended for Hezhong and memorialized, "Ke was originally a household slave of our clan; we beg that a great minister be chosen to guard Hezhong."
translations.idiomatic: Gong and his younger brother Yao, governor of Jiang, fought over Hezhong and memorialized: "Ke was originally a household slave in our family—we ask that a senior minister be appointed to govern Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 又與朱全忠書言之。

translations.literal: They also wrote to Zhu Quanzhong to the same effect.
translations.idiomatic: They also wrote to Zhu Quanzhong to the same effect.

sentences.zh: 珂急，乃遣使請婚於李克用。

translations.literal: Ke was anxious and therefore sent envoys to request a marriage alliance with Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: Ke, in desperation, sent envoys to seek a marriage alliance with Li Keyong.

sentences.zh: 克用薦之天子，許嗣鎮，然猶以崔胤為河中節度使。

translations.literal: Keyong recommended him to the Son of Heaven; permission was granted for him to succeed to the command, yet Cui Yin was still made military governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong recommended him to the throne, and the emperor approved his succession to the command, though Cui Yin was still named military governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 珙復構珂於王行瑜、李茂貞，曰：「珂不受代，且晉親也，將不利於公。」

translations.literal: Gong again framed Ke before Wang Xingyu and Li Maozhen, saying, "Ke will not accept replacement, and moreover he is allied by marriage with Jin—he will be harmful to you lords."
translations.idiomatic: Gong again slandered Ke to Wang Xingyu and Li Maozhen, saying, "Ke refuses to step aside, and as Jin's son-in-law he will work against you.

sentences.zh: 行瑜等約韓建共薦珙。

translations.literal: Xingyu and the others joined with Han Jian in jointly recommending Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu and the others joined Han Jian in recommending Gong instead.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「吾重已授珂矣。

translations.literal: An edict said, "I have already granted the command to Ke.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared, "I have already granted the command to Ke.

sentences.zh: 重榮有大功，不可廢。」

translations.literal: Chongrong rendered great merit—it cannot be set aside."
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong's great service cannot be cast aside.

sentences.zh: 行瑜怒，使其弟行約攻珂，克用遣李嗣昭援之，敗珙於猗氏，獲其將李璠。

translations.literal: Xingyu was angry and sent his younger brother Xingyue to attack Ke. Keyong dispatched Li Sizhao to reinforce him, defeated Gong at Yishi, and captured his general Li Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Xingyu sent his brother Xingyue against Ke. Keyong sent Li Sizhao to reinforce him; they defeated Gong at Yishi and captured his general Li Fan.

sentences.zh: 三鎮銜帝之卻其請也，連兵犯京師，謀廢帝、誅執政而立吉王，固請授珙河中。

translations.literal: The three commands resented the emperor's rejection of their request; they joined forces and invaded the capital, plotting to depose the emperor, execute the chief ministers, and install the Prince of Ji, and firmly requested that Gong be granted Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: The three commands, bitter that the emperor had refused them, marched together on the capital, plotting to depose the emperor, kill the chief ministers, and install the Prince of Ji, while insisting that Gong receive Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 克用聞之怒，以師討三鎮，瑤、珙兵引去。

translations.literal: When Keyong heard of it he was angry and led an army to attack the three commands; Yao and Gong's troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong was furious when he heard of it and marched against the three commands; Yao and Gong's forces withdrew.

sentences.zh: 克用拔絳州，斬瑤而屯渭北，敗行約於朝邑。

translations.literal: Keyong took Jiang Prefecture, beheaded Yao, and encamped north of the Wei; he defeated Xingyue at Chaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong captured Jiang Prefecture, executed Yao, and camped north of the Wei; he defeated Xingyue at Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 行約走京師。

translations.literal: Xingyue fled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyue fled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 弟行實在左軍，共說樞密使駱全瓘，謀挾帝幸邠。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xingshi was in the Left Army; together they persuaded the Commissioner of Military Affairs Luo Quanqiong to plot seizing the emperor and taking him to Bin.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xingshi served in the Left Army; together they persuaded Military Affairs Commissioner Luo Quanqiong to seize the emperor and take him to Bin.

sentences.zh: 右軍李繼鵬以告中尉劉景宣

translations.literal: The Right Army's Li Jipeng reported this to the superintendent Liu Jingxuan
translations.idiomatic: Li Jipeng of the Right Army reported this to Superintendent Liu Jingxuan

sentences.zh: （二人，茂貞黨也。），

translations.literal: (both men were partisans of Maozhen.),
translations.idiomatic: (both were partisans of Li Maozhen.),

sentences.zh: 欲以兵劫全瓘等，請帝幸鳳翔。

translations.literal: wishing to use troops to seize Quanqiong and the others and request that the emperor go to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: intending to seize Quanqiong and his allies by force and ask the emperor to go to Fengxiang instead.

sentences.zh: 兩軍合噪承天門街，帝登樓喻和之，繼鵬怒，輒射帝，縱火焚門，帝率諸王及衛兵戰，繼鵬矢及帝胄，軍乃退。

translations.literal: The two armies together clamored in Chengtian Gate Street. The emperor mounted a tower to admonish them toward peace. Jipeng was angry, shot at the emperor at once, and set fire to burn the gate. The emperor led the princes and guard troops to fight; Jipeng's arrow struck the emperor's helmet, and the army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Both armies raised an uproar along Chengtian Gate Street. The emperor mounted a tower to plead for peace. Enraged, Jipeng shot at the emperor and set the gate ablaze. The emperor led the princes and palace guards into battle; an arrow from Jipeng struck the emperor's helmet, and only then did the troops withdraw.

sentences.zh: 帝出幸定州將李筠軍，嗣延王戒丕、嗣丹王允以鹽州六都兵從帝出啟夏門，次於郊。

translations.literal: The emperor went out to the army of Ding Prefecture general Li Yun. The heir Prince of Yan, Jiepi, and the heir Prince of Dan, Yun, with the Six Commands troops of Yan Prefecture followed the emperor out through Qixia Gate and halted in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went out to the camp of Ding Prefecture general Li Yun. The heir Prince of Yan, Jiepi, and the heir Prince of Dan, Yun, led the Six Commands troops of Yan Prefecture with him through Qixia Gate and halted in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 兩軍憚鹽州兵銳，各走其軍。

translations.literal: The two armies feared the sharpness of the Yan Prefecture troops and each returned to its own camp.
translations.idiomatic: Both armies feared the Yan Prefecture troops' fighting edge and each withdrew to its own camp.

sentences.zh: 帝次莎城，百官繼至，士民從者亦數萬。

translations.literal: The emperor halted at Shacheng; the hundred officials arrived in succession, and civilians who followed also numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor halted at Shacheng; officials kept arriving, and tens of thousands of common people followed as well.

sentences.zh: 帝欲入谷中自固，以谷有「沒唐石」，惡之，徙石門。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to enter the valley to secure himself, but because the valley had a stone called "Tang-drowning Stone," he disliked it and moved to Shimen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to enter the valley to fortify himself, but because a stone there was called "Tang-drowning Stone," he took it as an ill omen and moved on to Shimen.

sentences.zh: 民匿保山谷間，帝每出，或獻飴漿，帝駐馬為嘗，民皆流涕。

translations.literal: The people hid and sheltered themselves among the valleys. Whenever the emperor went out, some would present malt syrup; the emperor would rein in his horse to taste it, and the people all wept.
translations.idiomatic: People hid in the valleys for safety. Whenever the emperor went out, some would offer malt syrup; he would rein in his horse to taste it, and the people wept as they watched.

sentences.zh: 既而遣嗣薛王知柔及劉光裕還京師。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he sent the heir Prince of Xue, Zhirou, and Liu Guangyu back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent the heir Prince of Xue, Zhirou, and Liu Guangyu back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 克用遣使者奔問行在，帝因詔克用、珂以兵趨新平，又詔涇州張鐇會克用軍以扼岐陽。

translations.literal: Keyong sent envoys in haste to inquire at the imperial camp; the emperor thereupon ordered Keyong and Ke to hurry troops to Xinping, and also ordered Zhang Fan of Jing Prefecture to join Keyong's army to block Qiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent envoys posthaste to the emperor's camp. The emperor then ordered Keyong and Ke to march on Xinping and directed Zhang Fan of Jing Prefecture to join Keyong's army and block Qiyang.

sentences.zh: 克用在河中未出也，帝懼茂貞之逼，復使嗣延王戒丕以禦服玉器賜之，督其西，乃壁渭北，進營渭橋。

translations.literal: Keyong had not yet left Hezhong. The emperor feared Maozhen's pressure, again sent the heir Prince of Yan, Jiepi, with imperial robes and jade vessels as gifts, and urged him westward; he then fortified north of the Wei and advanced to camp at Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong had not yet left Hezhong. Fearing Li Maozhen's advance, the emperor again sent the heir Prince of Yan, Jiepi, with imperial robes and jade vessels as gifts and pressed him to march west. Keyong fortified north of the Wei and advanced to camp at Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 於是行瑜壁興平，茂貞壁鄠。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xingyu fortified at Xingping and Maozhen at E.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu fortified at Xingping while Maozhen held E.

sentences.zh: 行瑜兵數卻，茂貞懼，斬繼鵬，傳首以謝。

translations.literal: Xingyu's troops were repeatedly driven back; Maozhen was afraid, beheaded Jipeng, and sent his head as an apology.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu's forces were repeatedly driven back. Maozhen, alarmed, executed Jipeng and sent his head as an apology.

sentences.zh: 繼鵬姓閻名珪，左神策軍拍張人，為茂貞養子雲。

translations.literal: Jipeng's surname was Yan and his given name Gui; he was a clapper-man of the Left Shence Army and had been adopted by Maozhen under the name Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Jipeng, surname Yan and given name Gui, was a clapper-man in the Left Shence Army and Li Maozhen's adopted son Yun.

sentences.zh: 詔削行瑜官爵，以克用為邠寧四面行營都招討使，珂為糧料使。

translations.literal: An edict stripped Xingyu of rank and titles, made Keyong overall pacification commissioner of the four-sided campaigning army of Bin and Ning, and Ke provisions commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped Xingyu of rank and titles, appointed Keyong overall pacification commissioner of the Bin-Ning campaigning army, and made Ke provisions commissioner.

sentences.zh: 克用遣子存貞請天子還宮。

translations.literal: Keyong sent his son Cunzhen to request that the Son of Heaven return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent his son Cunzhen to ask the emperor to return to the palace.

sentences.zh: 詔以騎三千戍三橋。

translations.literal: An edict ordered three thousand cavalry to garrison the Three Bridges.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posted three thousand cavalry to garrison the Three Bridges.

sentences.zh: 帝既還，加珂檢校司空，為節度使。

translations.literal: After the emperor had returned, Ke was advanced to acting Minister of Works and made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor had returned, Ke was promoted to acting Minister of Works and confirmed as military governor.

sentences.zh: 克用以女妻之，珂親迎太原，以李嗣昭助守河中，因攻珙，珙戰數北。

translations.literal: Keyong gave him his daughter in marriage; Ke went in person to Taiyuan to welcome her. Li Sizhao was sent to help guard Hezhong, and they then attacked Gong, who was defeated in battle several times.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong gave him his daughter in marriage, and Ke went to Taiyuan in person to fetch her. Li Sizhao helped defend Hezhong while they attacked Gong, who lost battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 珙任威虐，殺人斷首置前，而顏色泰定，下恐，不敢叛，然稍弱，無鬥誌。

translations.literal: Gong relied on ferocious cruelty; he would kill men and set severed heads before him while his countenance remained perfectly calm. His subordinates were afraid and dared not rebel, yet they gradually weakened and lost fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Gong ruled through savage cruelty, killing men and setting their severed heads before him while his face stayed perfectly calm. His men were terrified and dared not rebel, but they grew weaker and lost all will to fight.

sentences.zh: 光化二年，為部將李璠所殺，自為留後，詔代珙節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guanghua he was killed by his subordinate Li Fan, who installed himself as acting commissioner; an edict granted him the military governorship in Gong's place.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guanghua his subordinate Li Fan killed him, installed himself as acting commissioner, and received an edict replacing Gong as military governor.

sentences.zh: 又失眾，凡五月，為牙將朱簡所殺，挈其地入朱全忠，表授節度使、同中書門下平章事，更名友謙。

translations.literal: He again lost the support of the troops; within five months he was killed by garrison officer Zhu Jian, who surrendered the territory to Zhu Quanzhong. Quanzhong memorialized to appoint him military governor and Grand Councilor, and changed his name to Youqian.
translations.idiomatic: He soon lost the army's loyalty. Within five months garrison officer Zhu Jian killed him and surrendered the territory to Zhu Quanzhong, who memorialized to make him military governor and Grand Councilor and renamed him Youqian.

sentences.zh: 珙殺給事中王等十餘人，幕府遭戮辱甚眾，人有罪輒刳以逞。

translations.literal: Gong killed more than ten men including the Attendant Gentleman Wang, and many in the staff office suffered slaughter and humiliation; whenever anyone was guilty he would disembowel them to vent himself.
translations.idiomatic: Gong killed more than ten men including Attendant Gentleman Wang, and many staff members suffered slaughter and humiliation; he routinely disemboweled the guilty to satisfy his cruelty.

sentences.zh: 貨者，故為常州刺史，避難江湖，帝聞剛鯁，以給事中召，道出陜。

translations.literal: Huo Zhe had formerly been governor of Chang Prefecture; he took refuge on the rivers and lakes. The emperor, hearing of his firm uprightness, summoned him as Attendant Gentleman; his route passed through Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Zhe had once been governor of Chang Prefecture and had fled to the waterways for safety. Hearing of his stubborn integrity, the emperor summoned him as Attendant Gentleman; his route passed through Shan.

sentences.zh: 珙謂且柄任，厚禮之。

translations.literal: Gong supposed he was about to wield power and treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Gong assumed he was soon to hold high office and treated him with lavish courtesy.

sentences.zh: 鄙其武暴，不降意。

translations.literal: Huo despised his martial brutality and would not lower himself in manner.
translations.idiomatic: Huo despised his brutish violence and refused to defer to him.

sentences.zh: 既宴，盛列珍器音樂，珙請於貨曰：「仆今日得在子弟列，大賜也。」

translations.literal: After the banquet, with precious vessels and music arrayed in splendor, Gong requested of Huo, "Today I am permitted to stand among your younger kin—a great favor."
translations.idiomatic: At the banquet, with precious vessels and music displayed in splendor, Gong said to Huo, "Today I am honored to stand among your younger kin—a great privilege.

sentences.zh: 三請，貨不答。

translations.literal: He asked three times; Huo did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: He asked three times; Huo would not reply.

sentences.zh: 珙勃然曰：「天子召公，公不可留此。」

translations.literal: Gong flushed with anger and said, "The Son of Heaven summons you, sir—you cannot remain here."
translations.idiomatic: Gong flushed with anger and said, "The Son of Heaven summons you—you cannot stay here.

sentences.zh: 遂罷，遣吏就道殺之，族其家，投諸河，以溺死聞。

translations.literal: The feast was then ended; he sent officers to kill Huo on the road, exterminated his family, cast them into the river, and reported that he had drowned.
translations.idiomatic: The feast ended. He sent officers to kill Huo on the road, exterminated his family, threw the bodies into the river, and reported that Huo had drowned.

sentences.zh: 帝不能詰。

translations.literal: The emperor could not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was powerless to investigate.

sentences.zh: 珙死，贈太師。

translations.literal: When Gong died, he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: After Gong's death he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 詔陜州冤死者，有司吊祭，存問其家。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that those wrongfully killed in Shan Prefecture be mourned and sacrificed to by the authorities, and their families comforted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed officials to mourn and sacrifice for those wrongfully killed in Shan Prefecture and to comfort their families.

sentences.zh: 始，全忠擊楊行密不能克，諷荊、襄、青、徐等道請己為都統以討行密，帝猗違未報；

translations.literal: At first Quanzhong attacked Yang Xingmi but could not overcome him; he prompted Jing, Xiang, Qing, Xu, and other circuits to request that he be made overall commander to attack Xingmi. The emperor hesitated and did not reply;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Quanzhong had attacked Yang Xingmi without success and prompted the Jing, Xiang, Qing, Xu, and other circuits to ask that he be made overall commander against Xingmi. The emperor hesitated and gave no answer;

sentences.zh: 而珂與太原、鎮定等道亦請加行密都統，以討全忠。

translations.literal: while Ke together with Taiyuan, Zhen, Ding, and other circuits also requested that Xingmi be made overall commander to attack Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: while Ke together with Taiyuan, Zhen, Ding, and other circuits asked that Xingmi be made overall commander to attack Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 繇是兩罷之，全忠怨珂，不忘也。

translations.literal: therefore both requests were set aside. Quanzhong resented Ke and did not forget it.
translations.idiomatic: Both requests were denied. Quanzhong resented Ke and never forgot it.

sentences.zh: 帝為劉季述所廢，珂憤見言色，屢陳討賊謀。

translations.literal: When the emperor was deposed by Liu Jishu, Ke's anger showed in his words and expression; he repeatedly presented plans to attack the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jishu deposed the emperor, Ke's rage showed plainly in word and face, and he repeatedly urged plans to attack the rebels.

sentences.zh: 既反正，首獻方物，帝甚倚之。

translations.literal: After the restoration he was first to present local products; the emperor relied on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration he was the first to present tribute, and the emperor relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 而全忠以克用方強，不敢加兵。

translations.literal: But Quanzhong, because Keyong was then strong, did not dare send troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong, however, dared not attack while Keyong was still strong.

sentences.zh: 及王镕詘服，拔定州，而克用兵折，乃謂其將張存敬曰：「珂恃太原侮慢我，爾持一繩縛之。」

translations.literal: When Wang Rong submitted and Ding Prefecture was taken, and Keyong's military strength was broken, he then said to his general Zhang Cunjing, "Ke relies on Taiyuan and insults me—take a rope and bind him."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Rong submitted and Ding Prefecture fell, and Keyong's armies were spent, he told his general Zhang Cunjing, "Ke leans on Taiyuan and insults me—take a rope and bind him.

sentences.zh: 存敬以兵數萬度河，由含山襲，絳州刺史陶建釗、晉州刺史張漢瑜皆降，以何絪戍之，進攻珂。

translations.literal: Cunjing led tens of thousands of troops across the river, struck by way of Hanshan, and the governors of Jiang and Jin, Tao Jianzhao and Zhang Hanyu, both surrendered. He garrisoned the territory with He Yin and advanced to attack Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Cunjing crossed the river with tens of thousands of men and struck through Hanshan. The governors of Jiang and Jin, Tao Jianzhao and Zhang Hanyu, both surrendered. He left He Yin to garrison the region and marched against Ke.

sentences.zh: 全忠率師繼進，即劾珂交構克用，為方鎮生事，不可赦。

translations.literal: Quanzhong led his army in continued advance and at once impeached Ke for colluding with Keyong and stirring trouble among the frontier commands—unforgivable.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong followed with his main army and immediately impeached Ke for colluding with Keyong and stirring trouble among the frontier commands—an offense that could not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 珂乞師太原，為絪所迮，不能進。

translations.literal: Ke begged troops from Taiyuan, but was hemmed in by Yin and they could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Ke begged Taiyuan for troops, but Yin blocked them and they could not get through.

sentences.zh: 珂急使妻遺克用書曰：「賊攻我，朝夕見俘，乞食大梁矣。」

translations.literal: Ke in urgency sent his wife with a letter to Keyong, saying, "The rebels attack me; any day I may be captured—I shall soon be begging food in Daliang."
translations.idiomatic: In desperation Ke sent his wife to Keyong with a letter: "The enemy presses me; I may be captured any day—I shall soon be begging bread in Daliang.

sentences.zh: 克用答曰：「道且斷，往救必俱亡，不如歸朝廷。」

translations.literal: Keyong replied, "The roads are about to be cut; if I go to rescue you we shall both perish. Better to submit to the court."
translations.idiomatic: Keyong answered, "The roads will soon be cut. If I march to save you we shall both perish. Better submit to the court."

sentences.zh: 珂窮，遣使告李茂貞曰：「上初反正，詔藩鎮無相疑。

translations.literal: Ke, at his wits' end, sent envoys to tell Li Maozhen, "When His Majesty first restored the throne, he decreed that the frontier commands should not suspect one another.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Ke sent envoys to Li Maozhen: "When the emperor first restored order, he decreed that the frontier commands should not suspect one another.

sentences.zh: 而朱公不顧約，以攻弊邑。

translations.literal: Yet Lord Zhu disregarded the pact and attacks my exhausted commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lord Zhu has broken the pact and attacks my exhausted commandery.

sentences.zh: 弊邑亡，則邠、岐非君所保，天子神器斂手付人矣。

translations.literal: If my commandery falls, then Bin and Qi will not be yours to protect, and the Son of Heaven's sacred regalia will pass into another's hands with folded arms.
translations.idiomatic: If my commandery falls, you cannot hold Bin and Qi, and the Son of Heaven's regalia will pass into another's hands.

sentences.zh: 宜與華州韓公出精銳固潼關，以張兵勢。

translations.literal: You should join Lord Han of Huazhou in sending crack troops to secure Tong Pass and display military strength.
translations.idiomatic: You should join Lord Han of Huazhou in sending elite troops to hold Tong Pass and show military strength.

sentences.zh: 仆不武，公其惠我西偏地，以為扞守。

translations.literal: I am not martial—would you grant me the western districts as a defensive hold?
translations.idiomatic: I am no fighter—grant me the western districts as a defensive hold.

sentences.zh: 蒲，請公自有之。

translations.literal: As for Pu, I beg that you take it for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: As for Pu, I beg you to take it for yourself.

sentences.zh: 關西安危，國祚長短，系公此舉也。」

translations.literal: The security of Guanxi hangs in the balance; the length of the dynasty's fortune depends on this move of yours."
translations.idiomatic: The fate of Guanxi—and the dynasty's future—rests on what you do now.

sentences.zh: 茂貞不答。

translations.literal: Maozhen did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen did not answer.

sentences.zh: 珂益蹙，會橋毀，潛具舟將遁，夜諭守兵，無肯為用者。

translations.literal: Ke was pressed ever tighter; the bridge was destroyed, and he secretly prepared boats to flee. At night he urged the garrison troops, but none would obey.
translations.idiomatic: Ke grew ever more desperate. The bridge was destroyed, and he secretly prepared boats to flee. That night he urged the garrison to follow him, but none would.

sentences.zh: 牙將劉訓叩寢門，珂疑有變，叱之，訓自袒其衣曰：「茍有它，請斷臂自明！」

translations.literal: Garrison officer Liu Xun knocked at the bedchamber door. Ke suspected treachery and shouted at him. Xun bared his own garment and said, "If there is any other intent, I beg to cut off my arm to prove myself!"
translations.idiomatic: Garrison officer Liu Xun knocked at the bedchamber door. Ke suspected treachery and shouted at him. Xun bared his chest and said, "If I mean anything else, cut off my arm to prove it!

sentences.zh: 珂出，問計所宜，答曰：「若夜出，人將爭舟，一夫鴟張，禍系其手。

translations.literal: Ke came out and asked what plan was best. He answered, "If you go out at night, men will fight over the boats; one man may run wild and disaster will be in his hands.
translations.idiomatic: Ke came out and asked his advice. Xun said, "If you flee by night, men will fight over the boats; one unruly soldier could bring disaster on everyone.

sentences.zh: 如旦日，以情諗軍中，宜有樂從者，可則濟，否則召諸將行成以緩敵，徐圖所向，上策也。」

translations.literal: At daybreak, speak frankly to the army—some should be willing to follow; if so, you may succeed. If not, summon the generals to negotiate a truce to slow the enemy and plan your course gradually—that is the best plan."
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak speak frankly to the army—some may follow willingly. If so, you can escape. If not, summon the generals to negotiate a truce to slow the enemy and plan your next move—that is the best course.

sentences.zh: 珂然之。

translations.literal: Ke agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Ke agreed.

sentences.zh: 明日，登城語存敬曰：「吾於朱公有父子歡，君姑退舍，須公至，吾自聽命。」

translations.literal: The next day he mounted the wall and said to Cunjing, "Between Lord Zhu and me there is the affection of father and son. Withdraw for now; when he arrives I shall obey of myself."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he mounted the wall and told Cunjing, "Lord Zhu and I are like father and son. Withdraw for now; when he arrives I shall submit of my own accord.

sentences.zh: 乃執太原諸將並奉節印內存敬軍，豎大幡城上，遣兄璘與諸將樊洪等見存敬。

translations.literal: He then seized the Taiyuan generals and, presenting the commissioner's seal, admitted them into Cunjing's camp, raised a great banner on the wall, and sent his elder brother Lin and the generals Fan Hong and others to see Cunjing.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the Taiyuan generals, handed over the commissioner's seal to Cunjing's camp, raised a great banner on the wall, and sent his brother Lin and generals Fan Hong and others to meet Cunjing.

sentences.zh: 存敬解圍而戍以兵。

translations.literal: Cunjing lifted the siege and garrisoned the place with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Cunjing lifted the siege and left troops to garrison the city.

sentences.zh: 全忠自洛至。

translations.literal: Quanzhong came from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong arrived from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 全忠，王出也，始背賊事重榮，約為甥舅，德其全己，指日月曰：「我得誌，凡氏王者皆事之。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong was of the Wang clan; he had first turned against the rebels to serve Chongrong, and they agreed to be uncle and nephew by marriage. Grateful that Chongrong had preserved him, he pointed to sun and moon and said, "When I achieve my aim, every Wang who becomes king shall serve him."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was of the Wang clan. He had first deserted the rebels to serve Chongrong, and they pledged uncle-nephew ties by marriage. Grateful that Chongrong had saved him, he swore by sun and moon: "When I succeed, every Wang who becomes king shall serve him.

sentences.zh: 至是，忘誓言，過重榮墓，偽哭而祭。

translations.literal: By this time he had forgotten his oath; passing Chongrong's tomb, he feigned weeping and made offerings.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had forgotten his oath. Passing Chongrong's tomb, he feigned tears and made offerings.

sentences.zh: 次虞鄉，珂欲面縛牽羊以見，全忠報曰：「舅之恩，無日可忘。

translations.literal: When he halted at Yuxiang, Ke wished to present himself bound, leading a sheep in submission. Quanzhong replied, "My uncle's kindness—there is no day I can forget it.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuxiang, Ke wished to present himself bound with a sheep in submission. Quanzhong replied, "My uncle's kindness—I can never forget it.

sentences.zh: 君若以亡國禮見，黃泉其謂我何？」

translations.literal: If you meet me with the rites of a fallen state, what will the yellow springs say of me?"
translations.idiomatic: If you greet me with the rites of a fallen state, what will the dead say of me?

sentences.zh: 珂出迎，握手泣下，駢轡以入。

translations.literal: Ke came out to welcome him; they clasped hands and wept, and entered side by side with reins joined.
translations.idiomatic: Ke came out to welcome him. They clasped hands and wept, then entered side by side.

sentences.zh: 居旬日，以存敬守河中，舉珂室徙於汴。

translations.literal: After ten days he left Cunjing to guard Hezhong and moved Ke's entire household to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days he left Cunjing to guard Hezhong and moved Ke's entire household to Bian.

sentences.zh: 後令入覲，遣人賊之於華州。

translations.literal: Later he ordered him to come to court for audience, and sent men to kill him at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he ordered Ke to come to court and sent men to kill him at Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 自重榮傳珂，凡二十年。

translations.literal: From Chongrong's line through Ke, altogether twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: From Chongrong through Ke, the Wangs held Hezhong for twenty years in all.

sentences.zh: 諸葛爽，青州博昌人。

translations.literal: Zhuge Shuang was a man of Bochang in Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Shuang was a native of Bochang in Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為縣伍伯，令笞苦之，乃亡命，沈浮裏中。

translations.literal: He served as a district squad leader; the magistrate had him flogged harshly, so he fled and drifted among the villages.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a district squad leader until the magistrate had him harshly flogged; he then fled and drifted from village to village.

sentences.zh: 龐勛反，入盜中為小校。

translations.literal: When Pang Xun rebelled, he joined the band and became a junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Pang Xun rebelled, he joined the rebels as a junior officer.

sentences.zh: 勛勢蹙，率百餘人與泗州守將湯群自歸，累遷汝州防禦使。

translations.literal: When Xun's situation grew desperate, he led more than a hundred men together with the Sizhou defender Tang Qun to surrender, and was repeatedly promoted to defense commissioner of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun's cause collapsed, he led more than a hundred men with Sizhou defender Tang Qun to surrender and rose to defense commissioner of Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李琢討沙陀於雲州，表為北面招討副使。

translations.literal: When Li Zhuo campaigned against the Shatuo at Yun Prefecture, he memorialized to make Shuang deputy northern pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zhuo campaigned against the Shatuo at Yun Prefecture, he memorialized to appoint Shuang his deputy northern pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 徙夏綏銀節度使，檢校尚書右仆射。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be military governor of Xia, Sui, and Yin, and appointed acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military governor of Xia, Sui, and Yin and made acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 黃巢犯京師，詔率代北行營兵入衛，次同州，降賊，偽署河陽節度使，代羅元杲。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao invaded the capital, an edict ordered him to lead the northern campaigning troops of Dai to guard the capital. He halted at Tong Prefecture, surrendered to the rebels, and was falsely appointed military governor of Heyang in place of Luo Yuangao.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao invaded the capital, an edict ordered him to lead the Dai campaigning troops to defend the capital. He halted at Tong Prefecture, surrendered to the rebels, and was installed as military governor of Heyang in place of Luo Yuangao.

sentences.zh: 元杲者，本神策將，狀短陋，倚中官勢，剽財輸京師，凡鉅萬，人怨之。

translations.literal: Yuangao had originally been a Shence general—short and ugly in appearance—who relied on eunuch power to plunder wealth and send it to the capital, in sums of tens of thousands; people resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangao had been a Shence general—short and homely—who relied on eunuch power to plunder wealth for the capital in vast sums; the people hated him.

sentences.zh: 爽至，募州人戰，眾不從，相率迎爽，元杲奔行在。

translations.literal: When Shuang arrived, he tried to recruit the prefectural troops to fight; they would not follow, but instead went together to welcome Shuang, and Yuangao fled to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuang arrived he tried to recruit local troops to fight, but they refused and instead welcomed him en masse; Yuangao fled to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 爽間道奉表僖宗以自明，詔拜節度使。

translations.literal: Shuang sent a memorial by secret route to Emperor Xizong to clear himself, and received an edict appointing him military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang sent a secret memorial to Emperor Xizong to clear himself and received an edict confirming him as military governor.

sentences.zh: 李克用援陳許，道天井關。

translations.literal: Li Keyong was reinforcing Chen and Xu and would pass through Tianjing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong was marching to reinforce Chen and Xu by way of Tianjing Pass.

sentences.zh: 爽懼，不肯假道，出屯萬善。

translations.literal: Shuang was afraid and would not grant passage, but went out to camp at Wanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang was afraid and refused passage, deploying instead at Wanshan.

sentences.zh: 克用自河中趨汝、洛。

translations.literal: Keyong marched from Hezhong toward Ru and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong marched from Hezhong toward Ru and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 爽累授京師東南面招討諸行營副都統、左先鋒使，兼中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Shuang was repeatedly appointed deputy overall commander of the southeastern campaigning armies around the capital, left vanguard commander, and concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang was repeatedly appointed deputy overall commander of the southeastern armies around the capital, left vanguard commander, and concurrent Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 朱溫為賊守同州，爽率輕兵入之，溫偃旗設伏以待，爽謂賊遁，士解甲就舍，伏發，爽悉棄鎧馬奔還。

translations.literal: Zhu Wen was holding Tong Prefecture for the rebels. Shuang led light troops into it. Wen lowered his banners and set an ambush. Shuang thought the rebels had fled; his men doffed armor and went to quarters. The ambush struck; Shuang abandoned all armor and horses and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen held Tong Prefecture for the rebels. Shuang led light troops in. Wen lowered his banners and laid an ambush. Shuang thought the rebels had fled; his men stripped armor and went to rest. The ambush struck; Shuang abandoned armor and horses and fled.

sentences.zh: 至修武，為魏博韓簡擊敗之，不敢入。

translations.literal: When he reached Xiuwu he was defeated by Han Jian of Weibo and did not dare enter.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiuwu he was defeated by Han Jian of Weibo and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 簡留將趙文弁戍河陽，自攻鄆，時中和二年也。

translations.literal: Jian left the general Zhao Wenbian to garrison Heyang and himself attacked Yan—it was the second year of Zhonghe.
translations.idiomatic: Jian left general Zhao Wenbian to garrison Heyang and marched against Yan himself—it was the second year of Zhonghe.

sentences.zh: 河陽人誘爽，自金、商馳，復入之，厚禮文弁及戍人，還之魏。

translations.literal: The people of Heyang enticed Shuang; he galloped from Jin and Shang routes and re-entered the city, treated Wenbian and the garrison troops with great courtesy, and sent them back to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Heyang's people invited Shuang back. He raced in from the Jin and Shang routes, re-entered the city, treated Wenbian and the garrison with great courtesy, and sent them back to Wei.

sentences.zh: 於是爽攻新鄉，簡自鄆來，戰獲嘉西。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shuang attacked Xinxiang; Jian came from Yan, and they fought west of Huojia.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang then attacked Xinxiang. Jian came from Yan, and they fought west of Huojia.

sentences.zh: 簡陰窺關中，其下不悅，裨將樂彥禎間眾之隙，引其軍先還，故簡兵八萬自潰，相藉溺清水至不流。

translations.literal: Jian secretly eyed Guanzhong; his subordinates were displeased. The deputy general Yue Yanzhen exploited the rift among the troops and led his army back first; thus Jian's eighty thousand men collapsed of themselves, trampling one another into the Qing River until it would not flow.
translations.idiomatic: Jian secretly coveted Guanzhong, and his men were displeased. Deputy general Yue Yanzhen exploited the discontent and led his troops back first. Jian's eighty thousand men collapsed on their own, drowning one another in the Qing River until it ceased to flow.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔爽為東南面招討使，伐秦宗權，表李罕之自副。

translations.literal: The next year an edict made Shuang southeastern pacification commissioner to attack Qin Zongquan; he memorialized to make Li Hanzhi his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict made Shuang southeastern pacification commissioner against Qin Zongquan, with Li Hanzhi as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 爽雖興庸廝，善吏治，法令澄壹，人無愁咨。

translations.literal: Although Shuang had risen from menial service, he was skilled in civil administration; laws and orders were clear and uniform, and the people had no complaints.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shuang had risen from humble service, he governed well; laws were clear and uniform, and the people had no grievances.

sentences.zh: 擢累檢校司空。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Guangqi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Guangqi.

sentences.zh: 其將劉經與澤州刺史張言共立爽子仲方為留後，為蔡賊孫儒所攻，奔於汴，儒取孟州。

translations.literal: His generals Liu Jing and the Ze Prefecture governor Zhang Yan jointly installed Shuang's son Zhongfang as acting commissioner. They were attacked by the Cai rebel Sun Ru, fled to Bian, and Ru took Meng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His generals Liu Jing and Ze Prefecture governor Zhang Yan installed Shuang's son Zhongfang as acting commissioner. The Cai rebel Sun Ru attacked them; they fled to Bian, and Ru seized Meng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李罕之，陳州項城人。

translations.literal: Li Hanzhi was a man of Xiangcheng in Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanzhi was a native of Xiangcheng in Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少拳捷。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled in boxing.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was skilled in boxing.

sentences.zh: 初為浮屠，行丐市，窮日無得者，抵缽褫祗衼去，聚眾攻剽五臺下。

translations.literal: At first he was a Buddhist monk, begging in the markets; when a whole day brought nothing, he would strike his bowl, cast off his robe, and gather a band to raid and plunder below Wutai.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Buddhist monk, begging in the markets. When a whole day brought nothing, he would strike his bowl, cast off his robe, and gather a band to raid below Wutai.

sentences.zh: 先是，蒲、絳民壁摩雲山避亂，群賊往攻不克，罕之以百人徑拔之，眾號「李摩雲」。

translations.literal: Earlier the people of Pu and Jiang had fortified Mount Moyun to escape the turmoil; bands of rebels attacked but could not take it. Hanzhi with a hundred men stormed it directly, and the crowd called him "Li Moyun."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the people of Pu and Jiang had fortified Mount Moyun against the chaos; rebel bands could not take it. Hanzhi stormed it with a hundred men, and men called him "Li Moyun."

sentences.zh: 隨黃巢度江，降於高駢，駢表知光州事。

translations.literal: He followed Huang Chao across the Yangzi, surrendered to Gao Pian, and Pian memorialized to appoint him administrator of Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Huang Chao across the Yangzi, surrendered to Gao Pian, and was appointed administrator of Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為秦宗權所迫，奔項城，收餘眾依諸葛爽，署懷州刺史。

translations.literal: Pressed by Qin Zongquan, he fled to Xiangcheng, gathered his remaining followers, attached himself to Zhuge Shuang, and was appointed governor of Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by Qin Zongquan, he fled to Xiangcheng, gathered his remaining men, joined Zhuge Shuang, and was made governor of Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 爽伐宗權，即表以自副。

translations.literal: When Shuang campaigned against Zongquan, he at once memorialized to make Hanzhi his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuang campaigned against Zongquan, he immediately memorialized to make Hanzhi his deputy.

sentences.zh: 屯睢陽，無功。

translations.literal: He encamped at Suiyang and achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He camped at Suiyang but achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 又表為河南尹、東都留守，使捍蔡。

translations.literal: He was again memorialized to be metropolitan magistrate of Henan and eastern capital regent, charged with defending against Cai.
translations.idiomatic: He was again memorialized as metropolitan magistrate of Henan and eastern capital regent, charged with holding the line against Cai.

sentences.zh: 河東李克用脫上源之難，喪氣還，罕之迎謁謹甚，勞餼加等，厚相結。

translations.literal: Li Keyong of Hedong escaped the disaster at Shangyuan and returned in low spirits. Hanzhi received and greeted him with the utmost deference, entertained him with extra provisions, and formed a close bond.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong of Hedong escaped the Shangyuan disaster and returned in low spirits. Hanzhi received him with the utmost deference, entertained him lavishly, and formed a close bond.

sentences.zh: 罕之因府為屯，會孫儒來攻，罕之不出。

translations.literal: Hanzhi made the prefectural offices his camp. When Sun Ru came to attack, Hanzhi did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi made the prefectural offices his camp. When Sun Ru attacked, Hanzhi would not come out.

sentences.zh: 數月，走保黽池。

translations.literal: After several months he fled to hold Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he fled to Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 東都陷，儒焚宮闕，剽居民去。

translations.literal: The eastern capital fell; Ru burned the palaces and halls and plundered the inhabitants as he departed.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern capital fell. Ru burned the palaces and plundered the people as he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 爽遣將收東都，罕之逐出之，爽不能制。

translations.literal: Shuang sent generals to recover the eastern capital; Hanzhi drove them out; Shuang could not control it.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang sent generals to retake the eastern capital, but Hanzhi drove them out, and Shuang could not restrain him.

sentences.zh: 俄而爽死，其將劉經、張言共立爽子仲方，欲去罕之。

translations.literal: Soon Shuang died; his generals Liu Jing and Zhang Yan jointly installed Shuang's son Zhongfang, intending to remove Hanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shuang died. His generals Liu Jing and Zhang Yan installed Shuang's son Zhongfang and plotted to remove Hanzhi.

sentences.zh: 而罕之故與郭璆有隙，擅殺璆，軍中不悅。

translations.literal: But Hanzhi had long had a rift with Guo Qiu; he killed Qiu on his own authority, and the army was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi had long been at odds with Guo Qiu and killed him on his own authority, to the army's displeasure.

sentences.zh: 經間眾怒，襲其壁，罕之退保乾壕，經追擊，反為所敗，乘勝入屯洛陽苑中。

translations.literal: Jing exploited the soldiers' anger and attacked his fortifications; Hanzhi withdrew to defend Ganhao; Jing pursued, but was in turn defeated; seizing victory he entered and encamped in the Luoyang imperial park.
translations.idiomatic: Jing exploited the soldiers' anger and stormed Hanzhi's camp. Hanzhi fell back to Ganhao. Jing pursued but was routed in turn; Hanzhi pressed the victory and encamped in the Luoyang imperial park.

sentences.zh: 經戰不勝，還河陽。

translations.literal: Jing did not win in battle and returned to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jing could not win and withdrew to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 罕之屯鞏，將度汜，經遣張言拒河上，反與罕之合，攻經不克，屯懷州。

translations.literal: Hanzhi encamped at Gong and was about to cross the Si; Jing sent Zhang Yan to block the river bank; Yan instead joined with Hanzhi, attacked Jing without success, and encamped at Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi camped at Gong and prepared to cross the Si. Jing sent Zhang Yan to block the river, but Yan joined Hanzhi instead. Their attack on Jing failed, and they camped at Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 孫儒逐仲方，取河陽，自稱節度使。

translations.literal: Sun Ru drove out Zhongfang, took Heyang, and declared himself military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ru drove out Zhongfang, seized Heyang, and declared himself military governor.

sentences.zh: 俄而宗權敗，棄河陽走，罕之、言進收其眾，丐援河東，克用遣安金俊率兵助之，得河陽。

translations.literal: Soon Zongquan was defeated, abandoned Heyang and fled; Hanzhi and Yan advanced to gather his troops, begged aid from Hedong; Keyong sent An Jinjun leading troops to help them, and they obtained Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zongquan was defeated and fled Heyang. Hanzhi and Yan advanced to absorb his troops and begged aid from Hedong. Keyong sent An Jinjun with an army to help, and they recovered Heyang.

sentences.zh: 克用表罕之為節度使、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Keyong memorialized to make Hanzhi military governor and Grand Councilor of the Secretariat with equal standing.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong memorialized to appoint Hanzhi military governor and Grand Councilor of the Secretariat with equal standing.

sentences.zh: 有詔與屬籍。

translations.literal: An edict enrolled him in the imperial clan registers.
translations.idiomatic: An edict enrolled him in the imperial clan registers.

sentences.zh: 又表言為河南尹、東都留守。

translations.literal: He further memorialized to make Yan metropolitan magistrate of Henan and eastern capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized to appoint Zhang Yan metropolitan magistrate of Henan and eastern capital regent.

sentences.zh: 罕之與言甚篤，然性猜暴。

translations.literal: Hanzhi and Zhang Yan were very close, but Hanzhi was suspicious and violent by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi and Zhang Yan were very close, but Hanzhi was suspicious and violent by nature.

sentences.zh: 是時大亂後，野無遺稈，部卒日剽人以食。

translations.literal: At that time, after the great disorder, not a stalk was left in the fields, and his soldiers plundered people day by day for food.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, after the great disorder, not a stalk was left in the fields, and his soldiers plundered people day by day for food.

sentences.zh: 又攻絳州，下之，復擊晉州，王重盈欲出汴兵救，罕之解圍還。

translations.literal: He also attacked Jiangzhou and took it, then attacked Jinzhou. Wang Chongying wanted to send out Bian troops to rescue it, so Hanzhi lifted the siege and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked Jiangzhou and took it, then attacked Jinzhou. Wang Chongying wanted to send out Bian troops to rescue it, so Hanzhi lifted the siege and returned.

sentences.zh: 而言善積聚，勸民力耕，儲廥稍集。

translations.literal: Zhang Yan, however, was good at accumulating stores; he encouraged the people to put their strength into farming, and granary reserves gradually gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan, however, was good at accumulating stores; he encouraged the people to put their strength into farming, and granary reserves gradually gathered.

sentences.zh: 罕之食乏，士仰以給，求之無涯，言不能厭，罕之拘河南官吏笞督之；

translations.literal: Hanzhi lacked food, and his soldiers depended on Yan for supplies. His demands were endless, and Yan could not satisfy them, so Hanzhi detained Henan officials and beat them to press the demand.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi lacked food, and his soldiers depended on Yan for supplies. His demands were endless, and Yan could not satisfy them, so Hanzhi detained Henan officials and beat them to press the demand.

sentences.zh: 又東方貢輸行在者，多為罕之邀頡。

translations.literal: Moreover, tribute shipments from the east bound for the imperial encampment were often intercepted and seized by Hanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, tribute shipments from the east bound for the imperial encampment were often intercepted and seized by Hanzhi.

sentences.zh: 重盈反間於言，文德元年，罕之悉兵攻晉州，言夜襲河陽，俘罕之家。

translations.literal: Chongying sowed distrust between him and Yan. In the first year of Wende, when Hanzhi led all his troops to attack Jinzhou, Yan made a night assault on Heyang and captured Hanzhi's household.
translations.idiomatic: Chongying sowed distrust between him and Yan. In the first year of Wende, when Hanzhi led all his troops to attack Jinzhou, Yan made a night assault on Heyang and captured Hanzhi's household.

sentences.zh: 罕之窮，奔河東，克用復表為澤州刺史，領河陽節度使，遣李存孝、薛阿檀、安休休率師三萬攻言。

translations.literal: Hanzhi was reduced to desperation and fled to Hedong. Li Keyong again memorialized to make him prefect of Zezhou and acting military governor of Heyang, and sent Li Cunxiao, Xue Atan, and An Xiuxiu with an army of thirty thousand to attack Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi was reduced to desperation and fled to Hedong. Li Keyong again memorialized to make him prefect of Zezhou and acting military governor of Heyang, and sent Li Cunxiao, Xue Atan, and An Xiuxiu with an army of thirty thousand to attack Yan.

sentences.zh: 城中食盡，言納孥於汴求救，全忠遣丁會、葛從周、牛存節來援，戰沅河聚。

translations.literal: When food in the city was exhausted, Yan sent his wife and children to Bian to request rescue. Zhu Quanzhong sent Ding Hui, Ge Congzhou, and Niu Cunjie to aid him, and they fought at Yuanheju.
translations.idiomatic: When food in the city was exhausted, Yan sent his wife and children to Bian to request rescue. Zhu Quanzhong sent Ding Hui, Ge Congzhou, and Niu Cunjie to aid him, and they fought at Yuanheju.

sentences.zh: 休休不利，降全忠，存孝還。

translations.literal: Xiuxiu was unsuccessful and surrendered to Quanzhong, while Cunxiao returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuxiu was unsuccessful and surrendered to Quanzhong, while Cunxiao returned.

sentences.zh: 全忠更以丁會為河陽節度使，言歸洛陽。

translations.literal: Quanzhong then made Ding Hui military governor of Heyang, and Yan returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong then made Ding Hui military governor of Heyang, and Yan returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 罕之保澤州，數出鈔懷、孟、晉、絳，無休歲，人匿保山谷，出為樵汲者，罕之俘斬略盡，數百里無舍煙。

translations.literal: Hanzhi held Ze Prefecture and repeatedly raided Huai, Meng, Jin, and Jiang without a year of rest; people hid in mountains and valleys; those who came out as woodcutters or water-drawers were captured and killed by Hanzhi until nearly all were gone; for hundreds of li there was no smoke from hearth fires.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi held Ze Prefecture and year after year raided Huai, Meng, Jin, and Jiang. People hid in the hills; those who ventured out as woodcutters or water-carriers were captured and killed until scarcely any remained. For hundreds of li not a hearth fire showed.

sentences.zh: 克用遣罕之、存孝攻孟方立，拔磁州，方立戍將馬溉兵數萬戰琉璃陂，罕之禽溉，敗其眾。

translations.literal: Keyong sent Hanzhi and Cunxiao to attack Meng Fangli and took Ci Prefecture; Fangli's garrison general Ma Ji had tens of thousands of troops at Liuli Po; Hanzhi captured Ji and defeated his army.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent Hanzhi and Li Cunxiao against Meng Fangli and took Ci Prefecture. Fangli's garrison commander Ma Ji brought tens of thousands to fight at Liuli Po; Hanzhi captured Ji and routed his force.

sentences.zh: 大順初，汴將李讜、鄧季筠攻罕之，罕之告急於克用，遣存孝以騎五千救之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhun, Bian generals Li Dan and Deng Jijun attacked Hanzhi; Hanzhi urgently reported to Keyong, who sent Cunxiao with five thousand horsemen to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhun era, Bian generals Li Dan and Deng Jijun attacked Hanzhi. Hanzhi urgently appealed to Keyong, who sent Li Cunxiao with five thousand cavalry to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 汴士呼罕之曰：「公倚沙陀，絕大國。

translations.literal: Bian soldiers called to Hanzhi: "You rely on the Shatuo and cut yourself off from the great state.
translations.idiomatic: Bian soldiers shouted at Hanzhi: "You rely on the Shatuo and cut yourself off from the great state.

sentences.zh: 今太原被圍，葛司空入上黨，不旬日，沙陀無穴處矣！」

translations.literal: Now Taiyuan is besieged and Minister Ge has entered Shangdang—in less than ten days the Shatuo will have no hole to hide in!
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan is besieged now, and Minister Ge has entered Shangdang. Within ten days the Shatuo will have nowhere left to hide!

sentences.zh: 存孝怒，引兵五百薄讜營，呼曰：「我，沙陀求穴者，須爾肉以飽吾軍，請肥者出鬥！」

translations.literal: Cunxiao was enraged, led five hundred men to press Dan's camp, and shouted: "I am the Shatuo hole-seeker—I need your flesh to fill my army's bellies; let the fat ones come out and fight!"
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao was furious. He led five hundred men against Dan's camp and shouted: "I am the Shatuo with nowhere to hide! I need your flesh to feed my army—let the fat ones come out and fight!"

sentences.zh: 季筠引兵決戰，存孝奮槊馳，直取季筠。

translations.literal: Jijun led troops to decisive battle; Cunxiao charged with spear in hand, riding straight to seize Jijun.
translations.idiomatic: Jijun brought his troops to a pitched battle. Cunxiao charged with spear raised and rode straight at Jijun.

sentences.zh: 讜夜走，追至馬牢川，敗之。

translations.literal: Dan fled by night; they pursued to Malao River and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Dan fled by night. They pursued him to Malao River and routed his force.

sentences.zh: 克用討王行瑜，表罕之副都統，檢校侍中。

translations.literal: Keyong campaigned against Wang Xingyu and memorialized Hanzhi as deputy commander-in-chief and acting palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Keyong campaigned against Wang Xingyu, he memorialized Hanzhi as deputy commander-in-chief and acting palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 行瑜誅，封隴西郡王，檢校太尉、兼侍中。

translations.literal: After Xingyu was executed, Hanzhi was enfeoffed as Prince of Longxi, acting Grand Commandant and concurrent palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingyu was executed, Hanzhi was enfeoffed Prince of Longxi and made acting Grand Commandant and concurrent palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 罕之恃功多，嘗私克用愛將蓋寓求一鎮，寓為請，克用不許，曰：「鷹鹯飽則去矣，我懼其翻覆也。」

translations.literal: Hanzhi relied on his many achievements; he once privately asked Keyong's beloved general Gai Yu to seek a circuit for him; Yu made the request; Keyong did not agree, saying: "When hawk and falcon are full they leave—I fear he will turn against me.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi grew arrogant with his achievements and once privately asked Keyong's favorite general Gai Yu to secure him a circuit. Yu pleaded his case, but Keyong refused, saying, "When hawks and falcons are full they fly away—I fear he will turn on me.

sentences.zh: 光化初，昭義節度使薛誌勤卒，罕之夜襲潞，入之，自稱留後，報克用曰：「誌勤死，懼它盜至，不俟命輒屯於潞。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guanghua, Zhaoyi military governor Xue Zhiqin died; Hanzhi attacked Lu by night, entered it, declared himself acting regent, and reported to Keyong: "Zhiqin died; I feared another bandit would arrive, so without awaiting orders I encamped at Lu."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guanghua, Zhaoyi military governor Xue Zhiqin died. Hanzhi stormed Lu by night, seized it, and declared himself acting regent. He reported to Keyong: "Zhiqin is dead. I feared another raider would arrive, so without waiting for orders I occupied Lu."

sentences.zh: 克用遣李嗣昭先擊澤州，拘罕之家屬送太原。

translations.literal: Keyong sent Li Sizhao first to attack Ze Prefecture and detained Hanzhi's family, sending them to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent Li Sizhao to attack Ze Prefecture first and detained Hanzhi's family, sending them to Taiyuan.
