sentences.zh: 罕之攻沁州，執刺史、守將，送款於汴，全忠表罕之昭義節度使，命丁會援之；

translations.literal: Hanzhi attacked Qin Prefecture, seized the prefect and garrison commanders, and submitted allegiance to Bian; Quanzhong memorialized Hanzhi as Zhaoyi military governor and ordered Ding Hui to support him;
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi attacked Qin Prefecture, seized the prefect and garrison commanders, and submitted to Bian. Quanzhong memorialized him as Zhaoyi military governor and ordered Ding Hui to reinforce him;

sentences.zh: 與嗣昭戰含口，嗣昭不利，葛從周取澤州。

translations.literal: He fought Sizhao at Hankou; Sizhao was disadvantaged; Ge Congzhou took Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Sizhao at Hankou. Sizhao fared poorly, and Ge Congzhou seized Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭又攻罕之，罕之暴得病，不能事。

translations.literal: Sizhao again attacked Hanzhi; Hanzhi suddenly fell gravely ill and could not conduct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao attacked again. Hanzhi fell suddenly and gravely ill and could no longer command.

sentences.zh: 會代戍，全忠更以罕之節度河陽三城，卒於行，年五十八。

translations.literal: Hui replaced him in the garrison; Quanzhong reassigned Hanzhi to govern the three cities of Heyang; he died on the march at age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Hui took over the garrison. Quanzhong reassigned Hanzhi to govern the three Heyang cities, but Hanzhi died on the road at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 未幾，嗣昭復取澤州，以李存璋為刺史，進收懷州，攻河陽。

translations.literal: Before long Sizhao again took Ze Prefecture, appointed Li Cunzhang as prefect, advanced to take Huai Prefecture, and attacked Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Sizhao retook Ze Prefecture, installed Li Cunzhang as prefect, advanced to seize Huai Prefecture, and attacked Heyang.

sentences.zh: 汴將閻寶引兵至，嗣昭還。

translations.literal: Bian general Yan Bao led troops there; Sizhao returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bian general Yan Bao brought troops up, Sizhao withdrew.

sentences.zh: 始，儒去東都也，井闬不滿百室。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Ru left the eastern capital, wells and lanes did not reach a hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Ru had first left the eastern capital, fewer than a hundred households remained along the lanes.

sentences.zh: 言治數年，人安賴之，占籍至五六萬，繕池壘，作第署，城闕復完。

translations.literal: After Yan had governed several years, people relied on him in peace; registered households reached fifty or sixty thousand; he repaired moats and ramparts, built mansions and offices—the city walls and gates were restored whole.
translations.idiomatic: After several years under Yan's rule the people lived in peace again. Registered households rose to fifty or sixty thousand. He repaired moats and walls, built offices and mansions, and restored the city gates and towers.

sentences.zh: 全忠懼言異己，乃徙節天平，以韋震為河南尹。

translations.literal: Quanzhong feared Yan would oppose him, so transferred him to Tianping circuit and made Wei Zhen metropolitan magistrate of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong feared Yan would turn against him, transferred him to Tianping circuit, and made Wei Zhen metropolitan magistrate of Henan.

sentences.zh: 爽諸將無傳地者，言後嗣名全義。

translations.literal: Among Shuang's generals none had lands to bequeath; Yan's descendants took the name Quanyi.
translations.idiomatic: None of Shuang's generals had territory to pass on; Yan's descendants adopted the name Quanyi.

sentences.zh: 王敬武，青州人。

translations.literal: Wang Jingwu was from Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingwu was from Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 隸平盧軍為偏校，事節度使安師儒。

translations.literal: He belonged to the Pinglu army as a subordinate officer and served the military governor An Shiru.
translations.idiomatic: He belonged to the Pinglu army as a subordinate officer and served the military governor An Shiru.

sentences.zh: 中和中，盜發齊、棣間，遣敬武擊定。

translations.literal: During the Zhonghe era, bandits arose between Qi and Di, and Jingwu was sent to attack and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhonghe era, bandits arose between Qi and Di, and Jingwu was sent to attack and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 已還，即逐師儒，自為留後。

translations.literal: After he returned, he expelled Shiru and made himself acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: After he returned, he expelled Shiru and made himself acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 時王鐸方督諸道行營軍復京師，因承制授敬武平盧節度使，趣其兵使西。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Duo was directing the campaign armies of the circuits to recover the capital. Acting under delegated authority, he appointed Jingwu military governor of Pinglu and urged him to send his troops west.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Duo was directing the campaign armies of the circuits to recover the capital. Acting under delegated authority, he appointed Jingwu military governor of Pinglu and urged him to send his troops west.

sentences.zh: 及京師平，進檢校太尉、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, Jingwu was advanced to acting Grand Commandant and Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was pacified, Jingwu was advanced to acting Grand Commandant and Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 龍紀元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Longji.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Longji.

sentences.zh: 子師範，年十六，自稱留後，嗣領事。

translations.literal: His son Shifan, age sixteen, declared himself acting regent and succeeded to the post.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shifan, sixteen years old, declared himself acting regent and took over the command.

sentences.zh: 昭宗自以太子少師崔安潛領節度，師範拒命。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong himself wished to have the crown prince's junior tutor Cui Anqian hold the military governorship; Shifan refused the order.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong wished to appoint his crown prince's junior tutor Cui Anqian as military governor, but Shifan refused.

sentences.zh: 時棣州刺史張蟾迎安潛，師範遣部將盧弘攻之，弘與蟾連和。

translations.literal: At the time Di Prefecture governor Zhang Chan welcomed Anqian; Shifan sent his officer Lu Hong to attack him; Hong joined forces with Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Di Prefecture governor Zhang Chan went out to welcome Anqian. Shifan sent his officer Lu Hong to attack him, but Hong joined forces with Chan instead.

sentences.zh: 師範以金啖之，曰：「君若顧先人，使不絕其祀，君之惠也。

translations.literal: Shifan sent him gold, saying: "If you will consider my forebears and not let their sacrifices cease, that is your kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan sent him gold and said, "If you will honor my forebears and keep their sacrifices from ending, that is your kindness.

sentences.zh: 不然，願死墳墓。」

translations.literal: Otherwise I wish to die at their graves.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I would rather die at their graves.

sentences.zh: 弘少之，不為備，師範伏兵迎於路，部將劉莘斬弘，遂攻棣州。

translations.literal: Hong underestimated him and made no preparations; Shifan set an ambush along the road; his officer Liu Shen killed Hong; then he attacked Di Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hong took him lightly and made no preparations. Shifan ambushed him on the road; his officer Liu Shen killed Hong, and Shifan then attacked Di Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蟾請救於朱全忠，全忠馳使諭解，師範拔其城，斬蟾，而安潛不敢入。

translations.literal: Chan begged rescue from Zhu Quanzhong; Quanzhong sent a swift messenger to counsel reconciliation; Shifan stormed the city, beheaded Chan, and Anqian dared not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Chan appealed to Zhu Quanzhong for help. Quanzhong sent a swift envoy urging peace, but Shifan stormed the city and beheaded Chan. Anqian dared not enter.

sentences.zh: 師範喜儒學，謹孝，於法無所私。

translations.literal: Shifan delighted in Confucian learning, was scrupulously filial, and in the law showed no partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan loved Confucian learning, was scrupulously filial, and showed no favoritism in applying the law.

sentences.zh: 舅醉殺人，其家訴之，師範厚賂謝，訴者不置，師範曰：「法非我敢亂。」

translations.literal: His uncle killed a man while drunk; the family prosecuted; Shifan lavished bribes to appease them; the accusers would not relent; Shifan said: "The law is not something I dare to overturn.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle killed a man while drunk, and the victim's family brought suit. Shifan offered lavish bribes to settle the matter, but the accusers would not relent. Shifan said, "The law is not something I dare to overturn.

sentences.zh: 乃抵舅罪。

translations.literal: He then punished his uncle according to the crime.
translations.idiomatic: He then punished his uncle according to the law.

sentences.zh: 母恚之，師範立堂下，日三四至，不得見三年，拜省戶外不敢懈。

translations.literal: His mother was angry with him; Shifan stood below the hall; three or four times daily for three years he came but could not see her; bowing outside the door he did not dare slacken.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was furious with him. For three years Shifan stood below the hall three or four times a day and could not gain an audience. He bowed outside her door and never slackened.

sentences.zh: 以青州父母所籍，每縣令至，具威儀入謁，令固辭，師範遣使挾坐，拜廷中乃出。

translations.literal: Because Qingzhou was where his parents were registered, whenever a county magistrate arrived he prepared full ceremonial retinue to pay homage; the magistrate firmly declined; Shifan sent men to seize and seat him, bowing in the courtyard before letting him leave.
translations.idiomatic: Because Qingzhou was his parents' registered home, whenever a county magistrate arrived Shifan received him with full ceremonial retinue. When the magistrate firmly declined, Shifan had his men seize and seat him, bowed to him in the courtyard, and only then let him go.

sentences.zh: 或諫不可，答曰：「吾恭先世，且示子孫不忘本也。」

translations.literal: When some advised against this he replied: "I honor my forebears and also show descendants not to forget their roots."
translations.idiomatic: When some advised against this, he replied, "I honor my forebears and show my descendants not to forget where they came from."

sentences.zh: 全忠已並鄆州，遣兵攻師範，師範下之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong had already taken Yan Prefecture; he sent troops to attack Shifan; Shifan submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong had already taken Yan Prefecture and sent troops against Shifan, who submitted.

sentences.zh: 會全忠圍鳳翔，昭宗詔方鎮赴難，以師範附全忠，命楊行密部將朱瑾攻青州，且欲代為平盧節度。

translations.literal: When Quanzhong besieged Fengxiang, Zhaozong issued an edict the regional commanders to rush to the rescue; as Shifan was attached to Quanzhong, he ordered Yang Xingmi's officer Zhu Jin to attack Qingzhou, also intending to replace Shifan as Pinglu military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong besieged Fengxiang, Zhaozong ordered the regional commanders to the emperor's aid. Because Shifan was tied to Quanzhong, the court ordered Yang Xingmi's officer Zhu Jin to attack Qingzhou and intended to replace Shifan as Pinglu military governor.

sentences.zh: 師範聞之，哭曰：「吾為國守藩，君危不持，可乎？」

translations.literal: Hearing this Shifan wept and said: "I hold the frontier for the state; when the sovereign is in peril I do not hold fast—can that be right?
translations.idiomatic: When he heard this, Shifan wept and said, "I guard the frontier for the state. When the sovereign is in peril, how can I stand aside?

sentences.zh: 乃與行密連盟。

translations.literal: He then allied with Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: He then allied with Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 遣將張居厚、李彥威以甲槊二百輿紿為獻者，及華州，先內十輿，閽入覺，眾擐甲噪，殺全忠守將婁敬思。

translations.literal: He sent generals Zhang Juhou and Li Yanwei with two hundred carts of armor and spears disguised as tribute; at Huazhou they first brought ten carts inside the gate; the gate guards perceived it; the crowd donned armor and clamored, killing Quanzhong's garrison commander Lou Jingsi.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Juhou and Li Yanwei with two hundred cartloads of armor and spears disguised as tribute. At Huazhou they first sent ten carts through the gate. The guards detected the ruse; the men donned armor, raised a clamor, and killed Quanzhong's garrison commander Lou Jingsi.

sentences.zh: 是時崔胤方在華，閉門拒戰，執居厚還全忠。

translations.literal: At that time Cui Yin was at Hua; they shut the gates to resist; Juhou was seized and sent back to Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin was then at Huazhou. The city shut its gates and fought back, seized Juhou, and sent him back to Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 劉鄩襲兗州，入之。

translations.literal: Liu Ye attacked Yan Prefecture and entered it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ye stormed Yan Prefecture and took it.

sentences.zh: 師範亦潛兵入河南，徐、沂、鄆等十餘州同日並發。

translations.literal: Shifan also sent secret troops into Henan; Xu, Yi, Yan, and more than ten other prefectures rose on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan also sent covert troops into Henan. Xu, Yi, Yan, and more than ten other prefectures rose on the same day.

sentences.zh: 全忠使從子友寧率軍東討。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent his nephew Youning to lead an army east to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent his nephew Zhu Youning east with an army to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 是時帝還長安，故全忠並魏博軍屯齊州。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had returned to Chang'an; therefore Quanzhong combined the Wei-Bo army and encamped at Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had by then returned to Chang'an, so Quanzhong combined the Wei-Bo forces and camped at Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王茂章方以兵二萬合師範弟師誨攻密州，破之，以張訓為刺史。

translations.literal: Wang Maozhang was then with twenty thousand men joining Shifan's younger brother Shihui to attack Mi Prefecture; they broke it and made Zhang Xun prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maozhang was then leading twenty thousand men with Shifan's younger brother Shihui against Mi Prefecture. They took it and installed Zhang Xun as prefect.

sentences.zh: 進攻沂州，敗其兵，還青州，半舍而屯。

translations.literal: They advanced to attack Yi Prefecture, defeated its troops, returned toward Qingzhou, and encamped halfway.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced on Yi Prefecture, defeated its force, and withdrew toward Qingzhou, camping halfway back.

sentences.zh: 友寧方攻博昌，未下，全忠督戰急，友寧驅民十萬，負木石，築山臨城中，城陷，屠老少投屍清水，遂圍登州。

translations.literal: Youning was then attacking Bochang without taking it; Quanzhong pressed the battle urgently; Youning drove a hundred thousand civilians carrying timber and stone to build a mound against the city; the city fell; he slaughtered young and old and threw corpses into the Qing River; then besieged Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Youning was attacking Bochang but had not taken it. Quanzhong pressed him hard. Youning drove a hundred thousand civilians to carry timber and stone and build a mound against the walls. The city fell. He slaughtered young and old and threw the corpses into the Qing River, then besieged Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 茂章欲啖友寧，不肯救。

translations.literal: Maozhang wanted to let Youning be consumed and refused to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhang was content to let Youning be destroyed and refused to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，城破，友寧負勝攻別屯。

translations.literal: Before long the city fell; Youning pressed his victory to attack other camps.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the city fell. Youning pressed his victory against other camps.

sentences.zh: 茂章度汴軍怠，與師範合擊友寧於石樓，斬其首，傳於行密。

translations.literal: Maozhang judged the Bian army slack; he and Shifan jointly struck Youning at Shilou, beheaded him, and sent the head to Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhang judged the Bian army overconfident. He and Shifan jointly attacked Youning at Shilou, beheaded him, and sent the head to Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 全忠怒，悉軍二十萬倍道至。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was enraged and brought the full army of two hundred thousand by forced march.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was furious and marched his entire army of two hundred thousand by forced marches.

sentences.zh: 茂章閉營，伺軍懈，毀壁出鬥，還與諸將飲，訖，復戰。

translations.literal: Maozhang shut the camp, watched until the army relaxed, tore down the walls to sally forth, then returned to drink with the generals; when done he fought again.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhang held his camp, waited until the enemy slackened, broke down the walls and sallied out, then returned to drink with his generals and fought again when the cups were done.

sentences.zh: 全忠望見，嘆曰：「吾有將如是，天下不足平！」

translations.literal: Quanzhong saw it and sighed: "If I had a general like this, the realm would not be hard to pacify!
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong saw it and sighed, "If I had a general like this, the realm would not be hard to pacify!

sentences.zh: 於是退屯臨淄。

translations.literal: He then withdrew to encamp at Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew and camped at Linzi.

sentences.zh: 茂章畏全忠，乃斂軍而南，使李虔裕以五百人後拒。

translations.literal: Maozhang feared Quanzhong; he drew in his army and went south, sending Li Qianyu with five hundred men to hold the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhang feared Quanzhong, drew in his army, and marched south, leaving Li Qianyu with five hundred men as rear guard.

sentences.zh: 茂章解衣寐，虔裕呼曰：「追至，將軍速去！」

translations.literal: Maozhang removed his robe to sleep; Qianyu called: "Pursuers have arrived—general, flee quickly!
translations.idiomatic: Maozhang stripped off his robe to sleep. Qianyu called out, "Pursuers are here—general, flee at once!

sentences.zh: 茂章曰：「吾共決死。」

translations.literal: Maozhang said: "We have decided to die together."
translations.idiomatic: Maozhang said, "We have decided to die together."

sentences.zh: 虔裕固請，茂章乃去。

translations.literal: Qianyu urgently pressed him; Maozhang then left.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyu pressed him urgently, and Maozhang at last fled.

sentences.zh: 已而追至，虔裕一軍覆，茂章免。

translations.literal: Soon pursuers arrived; Qianyu's whole force was wiped out; Maozhang escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers soon caught up. Qianyu's entire force was destroyed, but Maozhang escaped.

sentences.zh: 全忠見虔裕，欲釋之，瞋目大罵而死。

translations.literal: Quanzhong saw Qianyu and wished to release him; Qianyu glared and reviled loudly, and was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong saw Qianyu and meant to spare him, but Qianyu glared and cursed him loudly and was executed.

sentences.zh: 張訓召諸將謀曰：「汴人至，師少，何以待之？」

translations.literal: Zhang Xun summoned the generals to plan, saying: "The Bian men are here; our troops are few—how shall we face them?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun called his generals together and said, "The Bian army is here and our force is small. How are we to face them?

sentences.zh: 眾請焚城而亡，訓曰：「不然。」

translations.literal: The crowd asked to burn the city and flee; Xun said: "That will not do."
translations.idiomatic: The others urged burning the city and fleeing. Xun said, "That will not do."

sentences.zh: 即封府藏，下縣門，密引兵去。

translations.literal: He at once sealed the treasury stores, lowered the county gates, and secretly led troops away.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed the treasury, closed the county gates, and quietly led his troops away.

sentences.zh: 汴軍見府庫完，德之，不追。

translations.literal: The Bian army saw the treasuries intact and admired this; they did not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian army found the treasuries intact, admired his conduct, and did not pursue.

sentences.zh: 全忠留楊師厚圍青州，敗師範兵於臨朐，執諸將，又獲其弟師克。

translations.literal: Quanzhong left Yang Shihou to besiege Qingzhou; he defeated Shifan's troops at Linqu, seized the generals, and also captured his younger brother Shike.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong left Yang Shihou to besiege Qingzhou, defeated Shifan's army at Linqu, seized his generals, and also captured his younger brother Shike.

sentences.zh: 是時，師範眾尚十餘萬，諸將請決戰，而師範以弟故，乃請降。

translations.literal: At that time Shifan still had more than a hundred thousand men; his generals asked for decisive battle; but because of his brother Shifan requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan still had more than a hundred thousand men, and his generals urged a final battle, but because of his brother he asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 全忠歸其弟，假師範知節度留後事，師範獻錢二十萬緡以謝軍。

translations.literal: Quanzhong returned his brother, temporarily left Shifan in charge as acting military governor, and Shifan presented two hundred thousand strings of cash to appease the army.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong returned his brother and left Shifan temporarily in charge as acting military governor. Shifan presented two hundred thousand strings of cash to appease the army.

sentences.zh: 汴將劉重霸執棣州刺史邵播，得其書八百紙，皆教師範戰守，全忠憚而殺之。

translations.literal: Bian general Liu Chongba seized Di Prefecture governor Shao Bo, obtained eight hundred sheets of his writing—all instructing Shifan in warfare and defense; Quanzhong feared this and killed Bo.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian general Liu Chongba seized Di Prefecture governor Shao Bo and found eight hundred sheets of his correspondence, all advising Shifan on attack and defense. Quanzhong feared Bo's influence and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 葛從周圍兗州，劉鄩不肯下，從周以師範命招之，乃盡出將士，開門降。

translations.literal: Ge Congzhou besieged Yan Prefecture; Liu Ye would not submit; Congzhou recruited him in Shifan's name; Ye then sent out all officers and soldiers and opened the gate to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou besieged Yan Prefecture, but Liu Ye would not yield. Congzhou summoned him in Shifan's name. Ye then sent out all his officers and men and opened the gates to surrender.

sentences.zh: 從周為辨裝，使詣汴，鄩但素服乘驢而往。

translations.literal: Congzhou supplied him with traveling gear and sent him to Bian; Ye wore only plain clothes and rode a donkey thither.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhou fitted him out for the journey and sent him to Bian. Ye went in plain clothes, riding a donkey.

sentences.zh: 全忠賜冠帶，辭曰：「囚請就縶。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong bestowed cap and belt; Ye declined, saying: "Your prisoner asks to be bound.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong offered him cap and belt. Ye declined, saying, "Your prisoner asks to be bound.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: He was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 既見，慰之，飲以酒，固辭。

translations.literal: After meeting, Quanzhong comforted him and offered wine; Ye firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When they met, Quanzhong comforted him and offered wine, but Ye firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 全忠笑曰：「取兗州，量何大邪？」

translations.literal: Quanzhong laughed: "To take Yan Prefecture—how great a matter is that?
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong laughed and said, "To take Yan Prefecture—how great a thing is that?

sentences.zh: 擢署都押衙，在諸舊將上。

translations.literal: He promoted him to chief military escort, ranking above the older generals.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Ye to chief military escort, ranking above the older generals.

sentences.zh: 諸將趨入，鄩一無讓，全忠奇之。

translations.literal: When the generals hurried in, Ye showed no deference at all; Quanzhong was struck by this.
translations.idiomatic: When the generals hurried in, Ye showed no deference at all, and Quanzhong marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，徙師範於汴，亦縞素請罪。

translations.literal: After more than a year Shifan was transferred to Bian; he also wore mourning white to beg pardon.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year Shifan was transferred to Bian, where he too came in white mourning garb to beg pardon.

sentences.zh: 全忠見以禮，表為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: Quanzhong received him with courtesy and memorialized him as Heyang military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong received him courteously and memorialized him as Heyang military governor.

sentences.zh: 既受唐禪，友寧妻訴仇人於朝，乃族師範於洛陽。

translations.literal: After receiving the Tang abdication, Youning's wife petitioned the court regarding her enemy; Shifan's whole clan was extinguished at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After he accepted the Tang abdication, Zhu Youning's wife appealed to the court about her enemy, and Shifan's entire clan was exterminated at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 先是，有司坎第左，告之故。

translations.literal: Earlier the authorities had dug at the left side of his mansion and informed him of the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the authorities had begun digging on the left side of his mansion and told him why.

sentences.zh: 師範乃與家人宴，少長列坐，語使者曰：「死固不免，予懼坑之則昭穆失序，不可見先人地下。」

translations.literal: Shifan then feasted with his family; old and young sat in rows; he told the envoys: "Death cannot be avoided; I only fear that if we are thrown into a pit the ancestral tablets will lose their order and we cannot meet our forebears underground.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan then held a feast with his family, young and old seated in order. He told the envoys, "Death cannot be avoided, but I fear that if we are thrown into a common pit the ancestral order will be lost and we cannot face our forebears underground.

sentences.zh: 酒行，以次受戮者二百人。

translations.literal: As wine circulated, two hundred were beheaded in succession.
translations.idiomatic: As the wine went round, two hundred were beheaded in turn.

sentences.zh: 孟方立，邢州人。

translations.literal: Meng Fangli was a man of Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Fangli was a native of Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 始為澤州天井戍將，稍遷遊弈使。

translations.literal: He began as garrison commander at Tianjing in Ze Prefecture and was gradually promoted to roaming patrol commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He began as garrison commander at Tianjing in Ze Prefecture and was gradually promoted to roaming patrol commissioner.

sentences.zh: 中和元年，昭義節度使高潯擊黃巢，戰石橋，不勝，保華州，為裨將成鄰所殺，還據潞州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhonghe, Zhaoyi military governor Gao Xun attacked Huang Chao; they fought at Shiqiao without victory; Xun held Huazhou but was killed by his deputy Cheng Lin, who returned to occupy Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhonghe, Zhaoyi military governor Gao Xun attacked Huang Chao and fought at Shiqiao without success. Xun held Huazhou but was killed by his deputy Cheng Lin, who then seized Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 眾怒，方立率兵攻鄰，斬之，自稱留後，擅裂邢、洺、磁為鎮，治邢為府，號昭義軍。

translations.literal: The troops were enraged; Fangli led an attack on Lin, beheaded him, declared himself acting regent, and on his own authority split Xing, Ming, and Ci as a circuit, making Xing the seat and naming it the Zhaoyi army.
translations.idiomatic: The army was furious. Fangli attacked Lin, beheaded him, and declared himself acting regent. On his own authority he split off Xing, Ming, and Ci as a separate circuit, made Xing his seat, and called it the Zhaoyi army.

sentences.zh: 潞人請監軍使吳全勖知兵馬留後。

translations.literal: The people of Lu asked the army supervisor Wu Quanxun to serve as acting regent in charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Lu asked the army supervisor Wu Quanxun to serve as acting regent in charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 時王鐸領諸道行營都統，以潞未定，墨制假方立檢校左散騎常侍、兼御史大夫，知邢州事，方立不受，囚全勖，以書請鐸，願得儒臣守潞。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Duo led the overall commander of the various circuits' campaigning armies. Because Lu was not yet settled, an ink edict provisionally made Fangli acting Left Regular Attendant and concurrent Grand Censor, in charge of Xing Prefecture affairs. Fangli would not accept it, imprisoned Quanxu, and wrote to Duo requesting that a Confucian scholar be sent to guard Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo then led the overall commander of the circuits' campaigning armies. With Lu still unsettled, an ink edict provisionally appointed Fangli acting Left Regular Attendant and concurrent Grand Censor to govern Xing Prefecture. Fangli refused, imprisoned Quanxu, and wrote to Duo asking that a Confucian scholar be sent to govern Lu.

sentences.zh: 鐸使參謀中書舍人鄭昌圖知昭義留事，欲遂為帥。

translations.literal: Duo sent his staff adviser, Secretariat Drafter Zheng Changtu, to oversee Zhaoyi affairs as acting commissioner, intending to become military governor himself.
translations.idiomatic: Duo sent his staff adviser, Secretariat Drafter Zheng Changtu, to oversee Zhaoyi as acting commissioner, intending to take the governorship himself.

sentences.zh: 僖宗自用舊宰相王徽領節度。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong himself appointed the former chief minister Wang Hui to head the military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong himself appointed the former chief minister Wang Hui as military governor.

sentences.zh: 時天子在西，河、關雲擾，方立擅地而李克用窺潞州，徽度朝廷未能制，乃固讓昌圖。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was then in the west; the Yellow River region and the passes were in turmoil. Fangli held territory on his own authority while Li Keyong eyed Lu Prefecture. Hui judged that the court could not control matters and firmly yielded the post to Changtu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was in the west; the Yellow River region and the passes were in chaos. Fangli held territory on his own while Li Keyong coveted Lu Prefecture. Hui judged that the court could not control the situation and firmly yielded the post to Changtu.

sentences.zh: 昌圖治不三月，輒去。

translations.literal: Changtu governed less than three months and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Changtu governed for less than three months and then left.

sentences.zh: 方立更表李殷銳為刺史。

translations.literal: Fangli again memorialized to make Li Yinrui prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Fangli memorialized again to appoint Li Yinrui as prefect.

sentences.zh: 謂潞險而人悍，數賊大帥為亂，欲銷懦之，乃徙治龍岡。

translations.literal: He said that Lu was perilous and its people fierce, and that great commanders had repeatedly been made rebels there; wishing to wear down their boldness, he moved the seat of government to Longgang.
translations.idiomatic: He said Lu was rugged and its people fierce, and that great commanders had repeatedly turned rebel there; to break their spirit he moved the seat of government to Longgang.

sentences.zh: 州豪傑重遷，有懟言。

translations.literal: The prefecture's leading families resented the move and spoke in opposition.
translations.idiomatic: The leading families of the prefecture resented the move and spoke out against it.

sentences.zh: 會克用為河東節度使，昭義監軍祁審誨乞師，求復昭義軍。

translations.literal: It happened that Keyong became military governor of Hedong; the Zhaoyi army supervisor Qi Shenhui begged for troops and sought to restore the Zhaoyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Keyong became military governor of Hedong, Zhaoyi army supervisor Qi Shenhui begged for troops to restore the Zhaoyi Army.

sentences.zh: 克用遣賀公雅、李筠、安金俊三部將擊潞州，為方立所破。

translations.literal: Keyong sent the three generals He Gongya, Li Yun, and An Jinjun to attack Lu Prefecture and was defeated by Fangli.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent generals He Gongya, Li Yun, and An Jinjun against Lu Prefecture, and Fangli defeated them.

sentences.zh: 又使李克修攻取之，殺殷銳，遂並潞州，表克修為節度留後。

translations.literal: He again sent Li Kexiu to attack and take it, killed Yinrui, then annexed Lu Prefecture, and memorialized to make Kexiu acting military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Kexiu to attack and take it, killed Yinrui, annexed Lu Prefecture, and memorialized to make Kexiu acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 初，昭義有潞、邢、洺、磁四州，至是，方立自以山東三州為昭義，而朝廷亦命克修，以潞州舊軍畀之。

translations.literal: At first Zhaoyi comprised Lu, Xing, Ming, and Ci—the four prefectures. By this time Fangli took the three eastern prefectures as Zhaoyi for himself, while the court also appointed Kexiu and granted him the old Lu garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Zhaoyi comprised Lu, Xing, Ming, and Ci. Now Fangli kept the three eastern prefectures as his Zhaoyi, while the court appointed Kexiu and gave him the old Lu garrison.

sentences.zh: 昭義有兩節，自此始。

translations.literal: From this time there were two Zhaoyi military governors.
translations.idiomatic: From this point there were two Zhaoyi military governors.

sentences.zh: 克修，字崇遠，克用從父弟。

translations.literal: Kexiu, courtesy name Chongyuan, was Keyong's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Kexiu, courtesy name Chongyuan, was Keyong's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 精馳射，常從征伐，自左營軍使擢留後，進檢校司空。

translations.literal: Skilled in mounted archery, he often followed on campaigns; from Left Camp army commander he was promoted to acting commissioner and advanced to acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in mounted archery, he often campaigned with Keyong; from Left Camp army commander he was promoted to acting commissioner and then acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 方立倚朱全忠為助，故克用擊邢、洺、磁無虛歲，地為鬥場，人不能稼。

translations.literal: Fangli relied on Zhu Quanzhong for aid, so Keyong attacked Xing, Ming, and Ci year after year without pause; the land became a battleground and people could not farm.
translations.idiomatic: Fangli relied on Zhu Quanzhong for support, so Keyong attacked Xing, Ming, and Ci almost every year; the land became a battlefield and farming ceased.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年，克修擊邢州取故鎮，進攻武安。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangqi, Kexiu attacked Xing Prefecture, recovered the old seat, and advanced against Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangqi, Kexiu attacked Xing Prefecture, recovered the old seat, and advanced on Wu'an.

sentences.zh: 方立將呂臻、馬爽戰焦岡，為克修所破，斬首萬級，執臻等，拔武安、臨洺、邯鄲、沙河。

translations.literal: Fangli's generals Lü Zhen and Ma Shuang fought at Jiaogang and were defeated by Kexiu; ten thousand heads were cut off, Zhen and others were captured, and Wu'an, Linming, Handan, and Shahe were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Fangli's generals Lü Zhen and Ma Shuang fought at Jiaogang and were routed by Kexiu; ten thousand heads were taken, Zhen and others captured, and Wu'an, Linming, Handan, and Shahe fell.

sentences.zh: 克用以安金俊為邢州刺史，招撫之。

translations.literal: Keyong appointed An Jinjun governor of Xing Prefecture to win the people over.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong appointed An Jinjun governor of Xing Prefecture to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 方立丐兵於王镕，镕以兵三萬赴之，克修還。

translations.literal: Fangli begged troops from Wang Rong; Rong sent thirty thousand men to his aid, and Kexiu withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fangli begged Wang Rong for troops; Rong sent thirty thousand men, and Kexiu withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後二年，方立督部將奚忠信兵三萬攻遼州，以金啖赫連鐸與連和。

translations.literal: Two years later Fangli supervised his subordinate Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand troops to attack Liao Prefecture, bribing Helian Duo with gold to join in alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Fangli led his subordinate Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand men against Liao Prefecture and bribed Helian Duo with gold to join him.

sentences.zh: 會契丹攻鐸，師失期，忠信三分其兵，鼓而行，克用伏兵於險，忠信前軍沒。

translations.literal: It happened that the Khitans attacked Duo; the army missed its rendezvous. Zhongxin divided his force in three and advanced with drums beating. Keyong ambushed in a defile and Zhongxin's vanguard was wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitans attacked Duo and the army missed its rendezvous. Zhongxin divided his force in three and advanced with drums beating. Keyong ambushed them in a defile and destroyed the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 既戰，大敗，執忠信，餘眾走，脫歸者才十二。

translations.literal: After the battle they were greatly defeated; Zhongxin was captured, the rest fled, and only twelve men escaped back alive.
translations.idiomatic: They were routed in battle; Zhongxin was captured, the rest fled, and only twelve men made it back alive.

sentences.zh: 龍紀元年，克用使李罕之、李存孝擊邢，攻磁、洺，方立戰琉璃陂，大敗，禽其二將，被斧锧，徇邢壘，呼曰：「孟公速降，有能斬其首者，假三州節度使！」

translations.literal: In the first year of Longji, Keyong sent Li Hanzhi and Li Cunxiao to attack Xing and assault Ci and Ming. Fangli fought at Liuli Po and was greatly defeated; his two generals were captured, put in cangue and stocks, and paraded before the Xing ramparts with the cry, "Lord Meng, surrender quickly! Whoever can cut off his head shall be made provisional military governor of the three prefectures!"
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longji, Keyong sent Li Hanzhi and Li Cunxiao against Xing and Ci-Ming. Fangli fought at Liuli Po and was routed; two generals were captured, shackled, and paraded before the Xing ramparts with the cry, "Lord Meng, surrender at once! Whoever cuts off his head shall govern the three prefectures!

sentences.zh: 方立力屈，又屬州殘墮，人心恐。

translations.literal: Fangli's strength was spent, and moreover the prefectures were ruined and collapsing; hearts were filled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Fangli's strength was spent, the prefectures lay in ruins, and panic spread through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 性剛急，持下少恩，夜自行陴，兵皆倨，告勞。

translations.literal: By nature he was harsh and impatient, showing little kindness to subordinates. He walked the ramparts by night himself; the troops were all insolent and complained of exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh and impatient by nature, he showed little kindness below. He patrolled the ramparts by night himself; the troops grew insolent and complained of exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 自顧不可復振，乃還，引冘殺。

translations.literal: Seeing that he could not rise again, he returned and took his own life by strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could not recover, he returned and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 從弟遷，素得士心，眾推為節度留後，請援於全忠。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Qian had long won the troops' hearts; the army installed him as acting commissioner and requested aid from Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Qian had long won the army's loyalty; the troops installed him as acting commissioner and begged Quanzhong for help.

sentences.zh: 全忠方攻時溥，不即至，命王虔裕以精甲數百赴之，假道羅弘信，不許，乃趨間入邢州。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was then attacking Shi Pu and did not come at once; he ordered Wang Qianyu with several hundred elite armored troops to hurry there. He asked passage through Luo Hongxin, who refused, and so entered Xing Prefecture by a hidden route.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was attacking Shi Pu and could not come at once; he sent Wang Qianyu with several hundred elite troops. Luo Hongxin refused passage, so they entered Xing by a hidden route.

sentences.zh: 大順元年，存孝復攻邢，遷挈邢、洺、磁三州降，執王虔裕三百人獻之，遂遷太原。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dashun, Cunxiao again attacked Xing. Qian brought the three prefectures of Xing, Ming, and Ci to surrender, seized Wang Qianyu and three hundred men and presented them as captives, and was then transferred to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dashun, Cunxiao attacked Xing again. Qian surrendered the three prefectures of Xing, Ming, and Ci, captured Wang Qianyu and three hundred men and sent them as captives, then was transferred to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 表安金俊為邢、洺、磁團練使，以遷為汾州刺史。

translations.literal: He memorialized to make An Jinjun training commissioner of Xing, Ming, and Ci, and Qian governor of Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to make An Jinjun training commissioner of Xing, Ming, and Ci and Qian governor of Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：以亂救亂，跋扈者能之；

translations.literal: The commentator says: To save disorder with disorder—only the overbearing can do that;
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: To quell disorder with disorder—only the overbearing can manage that;

sentences.zh: 以亂不能救亂，險賊者能之。

translations.literal: to fail to save disorder with disorder—only the treacherous bandit can do that.
translations.idiomatic: to fail at quelling disorder with disorder—only the treacherous bandit can manage that.

sentences.zh: 蓋救亂似霸，然而似之耳，故不足與共功。

translations.literal: Saving disorder may resemble hegemony, but it is only a resemblance; therefore one is not fit to share in great achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Saving a realm from chaos may look like hegemony, but it is only a resemblance—such men are not fit to share in great achievement.

sentences.zh: 觀王重榮寧不信哉！

translations.literal: Consider Wang Chongrong—is this not credible!
translations.idiomatic: Consider Wang Chongrong—can this not be believed!

sentences.zh: 破黃巢，佐李克用平京師，若有為當世者。

translations.literal: He broke Huang Chao and aided Li Keyong in pacifying the capital—one who seemed capable of achievement in his age.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Huang Chao and helped Li Keyong recover the capital—a man who seemed capable of shaping his age.

sentences.zh: 俄而奮私隙，逼天子出奔，雖馘朱玫，仆偽襄王，謂曰「定王室」，實卑之也。

translations.literal: Soon he gave rein to private quarrels, drove the Son of Heaven to flee, and though he slew Zhu Mei and toppled the false Prince of Xiang, Yun, calling it "settling the imperial house," in truth he debased it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he indulged private quarrels and drove the emperor to flee. Though he killed Zhu Mei and toppled the false Prince of Xiang, Yun, calling it "restoring the dynasty," in truth he diminished it.

sentences.zh: 身死部將手，救亂而卒於亂，重榮兩得之。

translations.literal: He died by a subordinate general's hand; he saved disorder yet ended in disorder—Chongrong gained both.
translations.idiomatic: He died at a subordinate's hands—he saved the realm from chaos yet died in chaos; Chongrong earned both outcomes.

sentences.zh: 不殺朱全忠，而為全忠誅，絕其嗣，宜矣。

translations.literal: He did not kill Zhu Quanzhong, yet was executed by Quanzhong and his line was cut off—as was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: He spared Zhu Quanzhong, yet was destroyed by him and his line extinguished—fitting enough.

sentences.zh: 余皆庸奴下材，無所訾責雲。

translations.literal: The rest are all mediocre men of servile talent—there is nothing to criticize or praise.
translations.idiomatic: The rest are mediocre men of servile talent—there is little worth praising or blaming.
